en: The Mahāyāna Mahāsannipāta Daśacakrakṣitigarbha Sūtra, Chapter One:
The Introduction, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.

Chapter One: The Introduction Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling on Mount Kailāsa, together with [a great assembly of] monks... (Note: The provided source text ends abruptly; the translation reflects the available portion.)
The Ṛṣi Niṣaṇṇa resided there together with a great assembly of bhikṣus— meaning a multitude of śrāvakas beyond measure—
and also with an assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas— meaning a multitude of bodhisattvas beyond measure.
Having thus spoken the Candragarbha [Sūtra], he said:
At that time, great clouds of incense came from the south, raining down a great rain of incense;
great clouds of flowers came, raining down a great rain of flowers;
great clouds of exquisite and magnificent jewel ornaments came, raining down a great rain of exquisite and magnificent jewel ornaments.
Clouds of great, wondrous, and pure garments arrive, raining down a great rain of wondrous, pure garments.
These clouds and rains fill the entirety of that mountain, the dwelling place where all the *muni* sages reside.
From all the fragrant flowers, precious ornaments, and garments, there issued forth hundreds of thousands of various subtle and wondrous sounds of the Great Dharma, namely:
the sound of taking refuge in and honoring the Triple Gem; the sound of receiving and upholding the precepts; the sound of patience and gentleness; the sound of diligent vigor and heroism;
the sound of subduing the four Māras; the sound of entering into wisdom; and the sound of vast renown.
The sound pervading the three realms; the sound exhorting the cultivation of sublime mindfulness, concentration, and dhāraṇī; the sound of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
the sound of revulsion toward craving and desire; the sound that form is like a mass of foam; the sound that feeling is like a floating bubble; the sound that perception is like a mirage;
the sound that formations are like a plantain tree; the sound that consciousness is like a magical illusion; [the sound of] non-existence...
The sound of permanence, the sound of suffering, the sound of non-self, the sound of emptiness, the sound of shame and remorse, the sound of seclusion, the sound of protective mindfulness,
the sound of loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity, the sound of realizing all dharmas, the sound of birth in heaven and nirvana,
the sound of proceeding toward the three vehicles, the sound of turning the great wheel of Dharma, and the sound of raining down the great rain of Dharma.
...the sound of maturing sentient beings; the sound of crossing over the three evil destinies; the sound of cultivating and perfecting the six pāramitās;
the sound of skillful means; the sound of entering the ten stages; the sound of sporting with supernatural powers;
the sound of sporting with the pure, unsurpassed Mahāyāna; the sound of the stage of non-retrogression; and the sound of the non-arising of phenomena...
The sound of patience, the sound of the consecration and reception of the throne, and the sound of entering the great ocean of all Buddhas.
At that time, the entire assembly that had gathered beheld such various clouds and rains, and also heard such sounds of the Dharma.
According to their respective inclinations and desires, each saw their own body adorned with various fragrant flowers, precious ornaments, and garments.

Furthermore, each saw a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*) held in the palm of both hands; from each of these wish-fulfilling jewels, various treasures rained down, and from each of these wish-fulfilling jewels, rays of light were emitted.
By means of that light, every sentient being beheld the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Furthermore, by means of that light, they saw each of the World-Honored Ones in those Buddha-lands, surrounded with reverence by immeasurable assemblies.

Furthermore, by means of that light, one sees all sentient beings in all Buddha-fields; if there are those who are ill, through being touched by the illumination of this light, their various ailments are healed and cured.
All those who were destined for execution or imprisonment attained liberation through the illumination of this light.
All the heavy, coarse, and turbid defilements of body, speech, and mind became light, supple, and pure because of the light; likewise, all who were hungry and thirsty were fully satisfied.
All those who were oppressed by various forms of punishment and affliction became free from sorrow and suffering because the light shone upon them.
All those who lacked clothing, precious ornaments, or wealth had their every need fulfilled according to their thoughts because the light shone upon them.

If there are sentient beings who desire to take life, or even those who desire to hold wrong views, through being touched by the illumination of this light, they all come to desire to distance themselves from taking life, and even desire to distance themselves from wrong views.

If there are sentient beings who are oppressed by the various sufferings of not obtaining what they seek, through the illumination of this light, they shall obtain everything according to their wishes.

Furthermore, by means of this light, one sees all the various sufferings endured by sentient beings in all Buddha-lands; none remain without rest, as they all experience joy and receive sublime bliss.

Furthermore, within these various Buddha-fields, by the touch of this light, all gloomy clouds, dust and mist, fierce winds, torrential rains, and unwholesome sounds were removed, as well as all foul odors, bitter and acrid tastes, unpleasant textures, and terrors;
all wrong actions, wrong speech, wrong thoughts, and wrong refuges were eliminated;
it was neither cold nor hot, peaceful and serene, with ground as level as the palm of a hand, and filled with every kind of exquisite object of enjoyment.
At that time, the bodies of those in the assembly suddenly felt as though the earth element had intensified; they became so solid and heavy that they were difficult to move.
Witnessing this auspicious omen, everyone was struck with wonder and doubt, asking:
"By what cause and by what condition has this sign appeared?"

In that assembly, there was a Śakra-devendra named Vimala-utpanna, who was seated not far from the Bhagavān. He rose from his seat, prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and questioned him with these verses:
“O Muni, who speaks the truth and possesses true vision, Who dwells perfectly in the truth— For the sake of the multitude, you have extensively proclaimed The ultimate, steadfast Dharma of truth.”
Since you cause all classes of sentient beings to extinguish suffering and the causes of suffering,
for what reason do you manifest clouds, rain, and the like within this world?
Causing the entire assembly to rejoice, they all gave rise to pure faith;
everyone set out upon the Mahāyāna, crossing over doubt and producing true vision.
The bodies of the great multitude of devas and humans, and the element of earth, increased in firmness and weight.
Unable to lift himself up— what is the cause of this sign?
Both hands manifest jewels, raining down various treasures and emitting light that illuminates the ten directions.
Purifying transgressions, ceasing suffering, and attaining peace and joy;
for what further reason, O Guide, do you cause the entire assembly to behold various fragrant garlands and other offerings, each adorning their own bodies?
Devas and humans are all filled with doubt, unable to fathom what the causes and conditions may be:
who is about to arrive, manifesting such supernatural power?
Is this a Buddha or a Bodhisattva?
"Are you Brahmā, Māra, Śakra, or a deva?
We pray only that the Great Teacher will swiftly proclaim this for the sake of the assembly!
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, Pure-Born, saying:

"You all should know that there is a bodhisattva-mahāsattva named Kṣitigarbha, who, throughout immeasurable and incalculable great kalpas, has brought sentient beings to maturity during the five turbidities in worlds devoid of Buddhas."

Now, together with eighty hundred thousand nayutas of kotis of bodhisattvas, he has come here for the purpose of paying homage, drawing near to, and making offerings to me; and because he wishes to observe this great assembly and give rise to sympathetic joy, he has brought his retinue along, appearing in the guise of śrāvakas, and has manifested these transformations through his supernormal powers.
"This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha is adorned with immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, and most excellent merits."
They cannot be fathomed by anyone in all the worlds, nor by śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.

This great bodhisattva is a treasury of all subtle and wondrous merits; a source from which the jewels of liberation emerge; the clear and pure eye of all bodhisattvas; and the foremost guide for merchants traveling toward nirvāṇa. Like a wish-fulfilling jewel, he rains down all manner of riches and treasures, satisfying everyone according to their aspirations.

It is like an island of jewels gathered by merchants; it is a fertile field for the growth of roots of goodness, a vessel for containing the joy of liberation, and a noble jar of merit from which wondrous treasures emerge.
Illuminating those who practice virtue, he is like the bright sun;
illuminating those who have lost their way, he is like a radiant torch;
removing the fever of afflictions, he is as cool as the moon.

It is like a vehicle for those without feet; like provisions prepared by one traveling a long distance; like a guide encountered by one who has lost their way; like a potent medicine taken by one who is deranged; like a skilled physician met by one who is ill; like a staff and cane relied upon by one who is frail and aged; and like a bed and seat where one who is exhausted may rest.
For those crossing the four floods, he acts as a bridge; for those proceeding toward the further shore, he acts as a boat or raft.
These are the sublime karmic fruits of the three roots of goodness, and they are the outflowing results induced by these three roots of goodness.

His constant practice of generosity revolves perpetually like a wheel; his steadfastness in maintaining ethical discipline is like Mount Sumeru; his diligence is indestructible like a diamond gem; his patience is immovable like the great earth; his meditative concentration is profound and secret like a hidden treasury; his meditative attainments are as magnificent as exquisite flower garlands; his wisdom is deep and vast like the great ocean; and he is free from all attachment, comparable to empty space.

The sublime fruit has near causes like the various flowers and leaves; it subdues all non-Buddhists like a lion king; it overcomes all celestial Māras like a great elephant; it slays the thieves of affliction like a divine sword; it avoids all clamor and bustle like the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddhas; it washes away the stains of affliction like pure water; it can eliminate foul odors like a swift gale; it severs the bonds of all fetters like a sharp blade; it protects against all fears like a kinsman or a friend; it wards off all enemies like a moat or a city wall; it rescues from all perils like parents; and it provides shelter for the timid and weak like a thicket of trees.

It is like a great tree by which one traveling far in summer takes refuge: it provides cool, clear water for those parched with heat; it provides various sweet fruits for those who are hungry and exhausted; it provides clothing for those who are naked; it provides great dense clouds for those oppressed by the heat; it provides a wish-fulfilling jewel for those who are destitute; it provides a place of refuge for those who are terrified; it provides sweet rain for all crops; and it provides moonstones for all turbid waters.

They cause the roots of goodness of all sentient beings not to be destroyed; they manifest wondrous realms to bring joy to the multitude; they exhort and inspire sentient beings to increase their sense of shame and remorse; and they cause those who seek merit and wisdom to be fully adorned.

It can eliminate afflictions like a purgative; it can collect a distracted mind like the object of meditative concentration (*samādhi*); its eloquence is unimpeded like water driving a wheel; it gathers phenomena and binds the mind like contemplating exquisite forms; its patient endurance is firm and stable like Mount Sumeru; its dhāraṇī is deep and vast like the great ocean; and its supernormal powers are unobstructed like empty space.
He eradicates all afflictive obscurations and their habitual tendencies, just as the scorching sun melts light ice.

He constantly dwells in the sublime path of the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) and the formless realms (*ārūpya*), and at the wondrous jewel-island of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), he effortlessly turns the great wheel of Dharma.
“Good son! This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha possesses such immeasurable, innumerable, and inconceivable, supreme merits as these.”
"Accompanied by his retinue, he wishes to come here; first, he has manifested such signs of supernatural power.
Having thus spoken of the various merits of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, the World-Honored One concluded.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, together with eighty, a hundred, a thousand, nayuta, and bimbara bodhisattvas, manifested the forms of śrāvakas through their supernormal powers and came from the south. Arriving before the Buddha, they stood there; together with their retinues, they reverently prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One, circumambulated him three times to the right, and stood before the Tathāgata with palms joined, praising him in verse:
"O Honored One among Two-Legged Beings, Guide, Your compassionate heart constantly covers all;
With patience like the great earth, You universally eliminate all anger and resentment."
Possessing the most excellent marks and signs, they adorn all Buddha-lands;
with true compassion, they fill all realms.
Having forever severed the net of all cravings, they dwell securely in accordance with reality.
Abandoning all pure lands, you deliver sentient beings mired in defilement.
By your original vow, you embrace this impure realm to bring wicked beings to maturity;
you rouse firm and correct diligence, having long practiced various ascetic austerities.
Having long practiced various austerities, he felt a heart of awe and trepidation upon hearing [the Dharma];
he cultivated all forms of giving, ethical discipline, patience, as well as diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
He once made offerings to and served immeasurable Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Śrāvakas.
And to rescue all sentient beings from hunger, thirst, disease, and death;
for the sake of other beings, he originally sacrificed his own many bodies and lives;
for the sake of the True Dharma, he sacrificed much bone, blood, and skin.
Relinquishing one’s own peace and happiness, out of compassion for all sentient beings,
one should diligently cultivate the severance of the net of afflictions solely for the sake of those beings.
Guarding the six sense faculties well, one should always remain far removed from all desires.
Contemplate that conditioned phenomena are impermanent, And that their nature is suffering, emptiness, and non-self.
All increasing afflictions and karmic actions Have craving and attachment as their cause;
Therefore, first regarding the six sense faculties, One must forever sever all greedy desires.
Throughout the entire realm of sentient beings, he dwells forever in great compassion;
though he has attained supreme enlightenment, he does not abandon his original vow.
Seeing all sentient beings oppressed by manifold sufferings, he [responds accordingly].
Exerting diligent effort as it arises, she courageously rescues and delivers them.
She causes them to diligently cultivate generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;
with a heart of loving-kindness, she nurtures them just as a mother does her only child.
Based upon the class of sentient beings, You have always maintained a mind of universal compassion;
Therefore, you swiftly realized Bodhi And delivered immeasurable multitudes.
In your original cultivation of the practices for enlightenment, There was nothing not done for the sake of living beings.
Therefore, regarding sentient beings now, I do not abandon the six perfections.
Having always sought unsurpassed bodhi in past末法 (mofa) eras,
I shall now likewise, within this末法 (mofa) age, swiftly achieve unsurpassed awakening.
Subduing all evil views, including those of devas, nāgas, humans, and yakṣas,
you abide securely and are able to sever delusions like the vajra-like noble path.
Bestowing [this path] upon immeasurable sentient beings, you grant them the prophecy of supreme bodhi.
He has become a worthy recipient of offerings and a leader, the most supreme and excellent field of merit.
The World-Honored One is without equal; he universally shelters all living beings, and his immeasurable fame fills the realms of the ten directions.
Therefore, all the bodhisattvas, in order to accomplish their own purpose,
have come together to take refuge at the feet of the Great Muni.
Hearing the sublime Dharma he proclaims, they all give rise to hearts of joy.
Exerting supreme diligence, they cultivate the practices of enlightenment.
Through the power of the Teacher’s Dharma, they shall all swiftly realize bodhi;
therefore, this present gathering of the Teacher is unprecedented and vast.
Thirteen trillion yakṣas, who constantly devour flesh and blood,
have all abandoned their evil karma and swiftly proceeded toward great enlightenment.
Some have attained supreme dhāraṇīs, as well as patience and meditative concentration.
There are those who have eternally exhausted all outflows, The World-Honored Ones worthy of offerings;
There are those who cultivate the four immeasurables, And those who abide in the four means of integration;
There are those who have attained the four analytical knowledges, And those who dwell securely in the patient acceptance of conformity.

Some have attained the Samādhi of Heroic Progress, some have obtained the eye of sublime wisdom, and some abide in the patience of the non-arising of phenomena; all are due to the power of the Teacher.
The World-Honored One of great majesty and virtue has utterly crushed the hosts of Māra’s enemies.
Having subdued all non-Buddhists, The ninety-five types of heterodoxies,
And exhausted the realms of hell-beings, animals, Hungry ghosts, and asuras— Therefore,
all sincere and steadfast sentient beings Return to the soles of your honored feet.
Now, having stilled the kalpas of war, pestilence, and famine,
you deliver all sentient beings who have lost their way in the darkness of blindness,
and who are maddened by various afflictions, establishing them all in the path of tranquil nirvana.
Therefore, having abandoned all other conditions, I have come to pay homage at the Venerable One’s feet.
From boundless Buddha-fields, all the current Guides extensively praise the World-Honored One; hearing this, they have all come here.
I have heard that the Ocean of the All-Knowing One possesses boundless and true virtues;
having delivered all sentient beings, I pay homage with a joyful heart.
Having cultivated immeasurable merit in the past, I now obtain the privilege of prostrating at the Venerable One’s feet.
May I, throughout immeasurable kalpas, Constantly practice manifold offerings.
Now, following the example of the World-Honored One, I make this solemn vow:
In this defiled land, May I attain unsurpassed bodhi.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, having praised the Buddha with sublime verses, together with his retinue, further took immeasurable celestial, exquisite incense, flowers, and various precious ornaments and scattered them over the Buddha; these transformed into a jeweled canopy and remained suspended in the air.
For the sake of hearing the Dharma, he sat upright and solemnly before the Buddha.

At that time, when the entire assembly who had gathered saw the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, they were all struck with wonder and attained what they had never experienced before; each took various kinds of exquisite incense, flowers, precious ornaments, garments, banners, pennants, and canopies, scattering them over the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha as an offering.
They all spoke these words:
"We have now gained a most excellent benefit; through the Buddha's spiritual power, we have been able to personally behold, pay homage to, and make offerings to such a Great Being."

At that time, there was among the assembly a bodhisattva-mahāsattva named Paripṛcchaka (Good Questioner). He rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, bared one shoulder, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"From where has this son of good family come?
How far is the Buddha-field where he dwells from here?
What kind of meritorious roots and virtues has he accomplished that he is thus praised by the World-Honored One in such various ways?"
Furthermore, how can you praise the inconceivable ocean of the Buddha’s meritorious dharmas?
We have never before heard or seen such a thing; we only pray that you will explain it for us.
The World-Honored One replied:
"Stop, son of good family!
Such are the merits and roots of goodness of this Great Being that all the world, including the great assemblies of gods and humans, cannot fathom the depth or extent of their measure."

If they were to hear the Tathāgata extensively expound such great merits and roots of goodness of this Mahāsattva, all the multitudes of gods and humans in the world would become bewildered and distressed, or perhaps fail to believe and accept it.
Then, Subhūti, having further requested with renewed earnestness, said:
"I only pray that the Tathāgata will, out of compassion, explain this for me.
The Buddha said:
"Listen attentively!
Reflect upon it well.
I shall briefly explain a small portion for you."
Such a Great Being has accomplished immeasurable, inconceivable, and preeminent merits;
he is already able to dwell securely in the supreme samādhi of Śūraṅgama and is well able to penetrate the realm of the Tathāgatas;
he has already attained the most excellent patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti) and has already attained mastery over all Buddha-dharmas.
They have already attained the capacity to endure the state of omniscience and have already crossed over the ocean of omniscience;
they have already become firmly established in the *siṃhavikrīḍitadhvaja-samādhi* (the samādhi of the lion’s playful stride banner) and are well able to ascend the mountain of omniscience;
they have already subdued the heterodox arguments of external paths and, desiring to bring all sentient beings to maturity, they dwell in every Buddha-land wherever they may be.

Such a Great Being, in whatever Buddha-fields they dwell and in whichever samādhis they abide, gives rise to immeasurable and sublime merits, thereby bringing immeasurable sentient beings to spiritual maturity.

"In this way, when such a Great Being dwells in any of these Buddha-fields and enters the meditative concentration that can generate wisdom, by the power of this concentration, he causes all sentient beings in those Buddha-fields to see, in common, the objective spheres traversed by all samādhis."

Abiding in such buddha-fields, if one enters the samādhi of the perfection of boundless wisdom, by the power of this concentration, all sentient beings in those buddha-fields will, according to their respective capacities, be able to reverently make offerings to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, with immeasurable and most excellent articles of worship.

Abiding in such buddha-fields as these, if one enters the samādhi of the perfection of pure wisdom, by the power of this samādhi, all sentient beings in those buddha-fields will simultaneously perceive the immeasurable faults and afflictions of all sensual desires, and their minds will attain purity.

Dwelling thus in these various Buddha-fields, if one enters the meditative concentration of wisdom endowed with shame and dread of blame, by the power of this concentration, all sentient beings in those Buddha-fields will attain fullness of superior shame and dread of blame, abandon all unwholesome dharmas, and their minds will be free from forgetfulness.

Abiding thus in these various Buddha-fields, if one enters the samādhi of the illumination that fulfills all vehicles, by the power of this concentration, all sentient beings in those Buddha-fields will attain skillfulness in the supernormal knowledge of the divine eye, the supernormal knowledge of recollecting past lives, and the supernormal knowledge of death and rebirth, thereby thoroughly understanding the causes and effects of this world and other worlds.

Abiding in such buddha-fields, if one enters the samādhi of the light of the supernatural power of freedom from sorrow, by the power of this concentration, all sentient beings in those buddha-fields will be made to leave behind all grief, anxiety, confusion, and mental darkness.

“Abiding thus in such Buddha-fields, if one enters the samādhi of the perfection of supreme supernormal powers and clear knowledge, by the power of this samādhi, all sentient beings in those Buddha-fields shall attain the perfection of skill in supernormal powers.”

Abiding thus in these various Buddha-fields, if one enters the samādhi that universally illumines all worlds, by the power of this concentration, one causes all darkness to depart from the realms of the ten directions, and causes all sentient beings in those Buddha-fields to see universally all the Buddha-fields of the ten directions.

Abiding in such buddha-fields as these, if one enters the samādhi of the Radiance of the Lamp-Torch of the Buddhas, by the power of this concentration, all sentient beings in those buddha-fields will abandon false refuges and take refuge in the Three Jewels of the True Dharma.

Abiding thus in these various Buddha-fields, if one enters the diamond-light samādhi (*vajraprabha-samādhi*), by the power of this concentration, all the minor Cakravāḍa mountains, the great Cakravāḍa mountains, Mount Sumeru, and all other mountains, as well as the ravines, gullies, pits, rubble, thorns, impurities, grasses, and trees within those Buddha-fields, shall completely cease to appear.

May all the various malevolent spells and poisons, evil insects and beasts, calamities and misfortunes, pestilences, darkness, dust and grime, impurities, and foul stenches within that Buddha-field be entirely extinguished.
He causes the ground of that Buddha-land to be as level as the palm of a hand, with all manner of auspicious signs spontaneously appearing, pure, sublime, and adorned with manifold marks.

Abiding in such Buddha-lands, if he enters the concentration called "The Power of Wisdom Difficult to Subdue," by the power of this samādhi, he causes all the Māras and their retinues in those Buddha-lands to be utterly terrified and to take refuge in the Triple Gem.

"Abiding in such Buddha-fields as these, if one enters the Samādhi of Lightning Radiance, by the power of this concentration, all sentient beings in those Buddha-fields will be made to remain far removed from the terrors of future lives and attain the consolation of the Dharma."

Abiding in such Buddha-fields, if one enters the concentration of the perfect and sublime flavor, by the power of this concentration, all sentient beings in those Buddha-fields shall, according to their thoughts, obtain food and drink in abundance.

Abiding in such buddha-fields, if one enters the meditative concentration of "endowed with supreme vital energy," by the power of this concentration, all sentient beings in those buddha-fields will, without exception, attain superior strength and vigor and be freed from all suffering of illness.

Abiding in such buddha-fields as these, if one enters the meditative concentration on supreme and exquisite requisites, by the power of this concentration, all sentient beings in those buddha-fields will, according to their wishes, obtain beds, seats, bedding, clothing, precious ornaments, and all physical necessities, lacking nothing; they shall be exceptionally wonderful and dignified, and most delightful.

Abiding in such Buddha-lands, if they enter the meditative concentration of the wisdom of non-contention (*araṇā-jñāna-samādhi*), by the power of this concentration, they cause all sentient beings in those Buddha-lands to have vigorous and robust bodies and minds; to be far removed from all enmity, hatred, and bondage; to be harmonious, joyful, and fully endowed with love and delight; and to practice generosity, ethical discipline, patience, heroism, and diligence, with minds free from distraction, thereby accomplishing wisdom.

"Abiding in such Buddha-fields as these, if one enters the concentration that induces supreme exultation, by the power of this concentration, all sentient beings in those Buddha-fields will experience immeasurable, sublime, and wondrous joy."

Abiding thus in these various Buddha-fields, if one enters the concentration known as "The Light of the Fulfillment of Worldly Paths," by the power of this concentration, all sentient beings in those Buddha-fields will attain unimpeded wisdom and be able to cultivate various kinds of pure activities.

Abiding in such buddha-fields as these, if one enters the Samādhi of the Supreme Well-Established Vajra, by the power of this samādhi, all sentient beings in those buddha-fields will have their sense faculties complete and without deficiency; they will always delight in seclusion, and their minds will be tranquil.

Abiding thus in these various Buddha-fields, if one enters the *samādhi* of the Supreme Banner of Superior Contemplation, by the power of this concentration, all sentient beings in those Buddha-fields will deeply revile and loathe the faults of their own evil karma, and they shall all skillfully uphold the ten paths of wholesome action, which is the essential path for rebirth in the heavens.

Abiding in such Buddha-fields as these, if one enters the samādhi of the Perfect Sound of Compassion and Mercy, by the power of this concentration, all sentient beings in those Buddha-fields will be caused to give rise to a mind of loving-kindness, a mind of compassion, a mind free from enmity and harm, a mind of universal equanimity, and a mind that seeks to mutually benefit and bring peace and happiness to one another.

Abiding thus in these various Buddha-fields, if one enters the concentration that draws forth and gathers all merit, by the power of this concentration, all sentient beings in those Buddha-fields will be freed from all strife, epidemics, famine, untimely winds and rains, and from suffering, astringency, pungency, acidity, and all evil forms and textures, which shall all be completely extinguished.

"In this way, when such a Great Being dwells in any of these Buddha-fields, if he enters the Samādhi of Oceanic Lightning, by the power of that concentration, he causes the entire ground of those Buddha-fields to be composed of various jewels; all calamities and afflictions are entirely removed, and it is universally adorned with various jewel-trees, clothing-trees, vessel-trees, various garland-trees, flower-trees, fruit-trees, various musical-instrument trees, and immeasurable musical instruments."

To speak briefly, this son of good family, every single morning, in order to bring sentient beings to maturity, enters meditative absorptions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; having arisen from those absorptions, he travels throughout the buddha-fields of the ten directions to mature all sentient beings who are to be converted, benefiting and bringing them peace and happiness according to their respective needs.
"This son of good family has, throughout immeasurable and incalculable great kalpas, brought sentient beings to maturity during the five turbidities in worlds devoid of Buddhas."
Furthermore, in the future, beyond even these numbers, there may be worlds where the kalpa of weapons arises and harms sentient beings.

Having witnessed this, this son of good family, at the time of dawn, by means of his powers of meditative concentration, will eliminate the kalpa of weapons and cause all sentient beings to regard one another with loving-kindness and compassion.
In some worlds, an eon of pestilence arises, harming all sentient beings.

Having witnessed this, these sons of good family, at the break of dawn, employ their powers of meditative concentration to eliminate the eon of pestilence, causing all sentient beings to attain peace and happiness.
In some worlds, a famine kalpa arises, harming all sentient beings.
Having witnessed this, this good son, at the time of dawn, through his powers of meditative concentration, eliminates the famine kalpa and causes all sentient beings to attain full satiety.
By means of his powers of concentration, this son of good family performs such immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable deeds for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings.

"This son of good family has fully accomplished immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, and supreme merits; he constantly exerts himself with diligence to benefit and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings."

In the past, before immeasurable, incalculable, and Ganges-sand-like numbers of Buddha-Bhagavāns, for the sake of bringing sentient beings to maturity and for their benefit, welfare, and happiness, you gave rise to great compassion and made firm, indestructible, courageous, and diligent vows that are inexhaustible.

By the superior power of this great compassion—firm and indestructible, courageous, diligent, and characterized by inexhaustible vows—one can, in a single day and night, or even during the duration of a single meal, deliver immeasurable hundreds, thousands, koṭis, and nayutas of sentient beings, causing them all to be liberated from various sorrows and sufferings, and ensuring that all their righteous aspirations and desires are fulfilled.
"Wherever there may be sentient beings who are oppressed by various longings, sorrows, and sufferings, if they are able to sincerely invoke the name,

recite the mantra, take refuge in, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, all shall obtain whatever they seek according to the Dharma and be freed from all sorrows and sufferings."
According to what is appropriate for each, they establish them upon the path to rebirth in heaven or to nirvāṇa.
In whatever place there may be sentient beings oppressed by hunger and thirst,

if there are those who with a sincere heart invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge in, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, all shall obtain whatever they seek according to the Dharma, and their food and drink shall be fully provided.
According to their respective needs, they establish them upon the path to rebirth in heaven or to *nirvāṇa*.

In whatever place there may be sentient beings who lack various garments, precious ornaments, medicines, bedding, and other necessities of life—if there are those who can with a sincere heart invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge in, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha—all shall obtain whatever they seek in accordance with the Dharma. Garments, precious ornaments, medicines, bedding, and all such requisites will be provided in full, and according to their respective needs, they shall be established upon the path to rebirth in heaven or to *nirvāṇa*.

In whatever place there may be sentient beings who long for separation from those they love or encounter those they hate, if there are any who can with a sincere heart invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge in, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, all shall attain the union of those they love and the separation from those they hate; furthermore, according to their respective needs, they shall be established upon the path to rebirth in heaven or to Nirvāṇa.
"In whatever place there may be sentient beings whose bodies and minds are afflicted by sorrow and suffering, or tormented by various illnesses;

if there are those who can with a sincere heart invoke the name, recite [mantras], take refuge, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, they shall all attain peace and happiness of body and mind, and their various illnesses shall be cured. Furthermore, according to their respective capacities, they shall be established upon the path to rebirth in the heavens or the way of Nirvāṇa."

In whatever place there may be sentient beings who are at odds with one another and engage in various forms of strife and contention, if there are those who can, with a sincere heart, invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge in, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, they shall all abandon their malicious and harmful intentions. They will instead become harmonious with one another, joyfully enduring and patient, repeatedly feeling remorse and shame, and turning toward each other with a heart of loving-kindness. Accordingly, they shall be established upon the path to rebirth in heaven or to Nirvāṇa.

In whatever place there may be sentient beings confined in prisons, shackled with manacles, fetters, or stocks, and subjected to all manner of suffering—if they are able to single-mindedly invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge in, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, they shall all attain liberation from their prisons, manacles, and fetters. They will be joyful and at ease, and according to their respective capacities, they shall be established upon the path to rebirth in heaven or to *nirvāṇa*.

In whatever place there may be sentient beings who are about to be imprisoned, flogged, tortured, or subjected to lethal harm, if there are those who can with a sincere heart invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge in, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, they shall all be liberated from imprisonment, flogging, and injury; and according to their respective capacities, they shall be established upon the path to rebirth in heaven or to Nirvāṇa.
"In whatever place there may be sentient beings whose bodies and minds are weary and whose physical strength is exhausted and diminished;

if there are those who can with a sincere heart invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge in, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, they shall all attain ease and comfort in body and mind, and their physical strength shall become robust. According to their respective capacities, they shall be established upon the path to rebirth in heaven or to Nirvāṇa."

In whatever place there may be sentient beings whose faculties are incomplete or impaired, if they can with a sincere heart invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge in, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, they shall all have their faculties restored and free from impairment; according to their respective capacities, they shall be established upon the path to rebirth in heaven or to Nirvāṇa.
In whatever place there may be sentient beings who are deranged, mentally disturbed, or possessed by malevolent spirits;

if they can with a sincere heart invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge in, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, all shall attain a mind free from madness and confusion, be liberated from all disturbances and afflictions, and, according to their respective capacities, be established upon the path to rebirth in heaven or to Nirvāṇa.

In whatever place there may be sentient beings whose greed, anger, delusion, resentment, stinginess, envy, pride, wrong views, sloth, negligence, and doubt are all intensely blazing, afflicting their bodies and minds so that they are never at peace or happy—if there are those who can with a sincere heart invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge in, revere, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, they shall all be freed from greed and the like, attaining peace and happiness of body and mind; and according to their respective capacities, they shall be established upon the path to rebirth in the heavens or to Nirvāṇa.

In whatever place there may be sentient beings who are burned by fire, drowned by water, or blown about by wind; or those who, upon mountain crags, precipices, cliffs, or riverbanks, fall from trees or houses, their hearts filled with terror—if they can with sincere heart invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge in, and pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, all shall escape every peril and remain safe and unharmed.
According to their respective needs, they establish them upon the path to rebirth in heaven or to nirvāṇa.
"In whatever place there may be sentient beings who are bitten by various venomous snakes or insects, or struck by various kinds of poisons;

if there are those who can with a sincere heart invoke the name, recite [his mantra], take refuge in, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, all shall be freed from every affliction and harm, and according to their respective needs, be established upon the path to rebirth in heaven or to nirvāṇa."

In whatever place there may be sentient beings who are possessed by malevolent spirits and afflicted with various types of malaria—whether it manifests daily, every other day, or once every three or four days—or who are driven to madness, whose bodies and minds tremble, who are bewildered and lose mindfulness, and who lack all understanding:

if there are those who, with a sincere heart, invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge in, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, they shall all attain liberation from fear; their bodies and minds will become peaceful and at ease, and they will be established, according to their respective needs, upon the path to rebirth in heaven or to Nirvāṇa.

In whatever place there may be sentient beings who are beset by yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, putanas, kumbhāṇḍas, kaṭapūtanas, and spirits that suck vitality; or by tigers, wolves, lions, and other ferocious beasts; or by malevolent poisons, curses, and various evil incantations; or by enemies, thieves, and military arrays; or by any other various causes of fear—they become terrified in body and mind, fearing for their lives, loathing death and craving life, and wearying of suffering while seeking happiness.

Should there be anyone who, with a sincere heart, invokes the name, recites the mantra, takes refuge in, honors, and makes offerings to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, all shall be freed from every fear, preserve their lives, and—according to their respective needs—be established upon the path to rebirth in heaven or to Nirvāṇa.
"In whatever place there may be sentient beings who, for the sake of extensive learning,
or pure faith, or pure ethical discipline, or meditative concentration, or supernormal powers, or wisdom, or liberation,
or exquisite form, or exquisite sound, or exquisite fragrance..."
...or for exquisite flavors, or for exquisite tactile sensations, or for gain and offerings, or for fame and reputation,
or for spiritual merit, or for crafts and skills, or for flowers and fruits,
or for groves and forests, or for beds and seats, or for bedding and furnishings, or for roads, or for wealth and grain.
...or as medicine, or as dwellings, or as servants, or as pigments,
or as sweet rain, or for the seeking of water, or for the cultivation of crops,
or as fans and whisks, or as cool breezes, or for the seeking of fire, or as vehicles, or as sons and daughters.
Whether for the sake of skillful means, or for the cultivation of merit, or for warmth, or for coolness, or for mindfulness,
or for various worldly and supramundane matters of benefit and happiness—
at the time of pursuing these, one is tormented by various forms of anxiety and suffering;

If there are those who, with a sincere heart, invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, then by virtue of this son of good family’s merit, wondrous samādhi, and majestic spiritual power, all such beings shall be freed from sorrow and suffering; their wishes and aspirations will be fulfilled, and they shall be established, as appropriate, upon the path to rebirth in heaven or the way of nirvāṇa.

"In whatever place there may be sentient beings who plant various seeds in wasteland or fertile fields— whether they are diligently engaged in cultivation or not— if they are able to single-mindedly invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge in,

and make offerings to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, then by virtue of this son of good family’s merit, wondrous concentration, and majestic spiritual power, all those fruits and grains shall become abundant."

Why is this? This son of good family, having passed through immeasurable and incalculable great eons, made firm vows of great diligence before Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, in numbers beyond reckoning. By the power of these vows, for the sake of bringing all sentient beings to maturity, he constantly and universally sustains the entire earth, constantly and universally sustains all seeds, and constantly and universally causes all those sentient beings to enjoy them as they wish.

By the power of this son of good family’s majestic spiritual authority, he is able to cause all things upon the great earth—grasses, trees, roots, rhizomes, sprouts, stems, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits—to grow and flourish; medicinal herbs, grains, crops, flowers, and fruits ripen to their full maturity, becoming moist, fragrant, pure, soft, and delicious.

"Wherever there may be sentient beings who, because their greed, anger, and delusion are all so fierce and intense, commit the ten paths of unwholesome action—namely, killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, harsh speech, divisive speech, frivolous speech, greed, anger, or wrong views—if there are those who can with a sincere heart invoke the name, recite the mantra, take refuge in, revere, and make offerings to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, all their afflictions will be completely extinguished;
they will distance themselves from the ten unwholesome actions, accomplish the ten wholesome actions, and give rise toward all sentient beings to a mind of compassion and a mind of benefit."

This son of noble family, having accomplished such merit, sublime meditative concentration, and power of majestic spirit, as well as valor and diligence, is able—in the duration of a single meal—to liberate immeasurable and innumerable sentient beings to be converted in each of countless and infinite Buddha-fields. Within that single meal’s time, he causes them all to be free from every suffering and attain peace and happiness, establishing them, according to their respective needs, upon the paths of rebirth in heaven or nirvana.
"This son of good family has accomplished such inconceivable dharmas of merit as I have described, as well as firm vows, heroism, and diligence."

In order to bring all sentient beings to maturity, he may at times manifest in the form of Mahābrahmā throughout the worlds of the ten directions, preaching the Dharma to sentient beings according to their needs.
Alternatively, he may manifest as the body of Maheśvara, or as the body of a Paranirmita-vaśavartin deity in the desire realm,
or as the body of a Nirmāṇarati deity, or as the body of a Tuṣita deity,
or as the body of a Yāma deity, or as the body of Śakra, or as the body of a Cāturmahārājika deity, or...
They may manifest as the body of a Buddha, or the body of a Bodhisattva,
or the body of a Pratyekabuddha, or the body of a Śrāvaka, or the body of a Cakravartin king, or the body of a Kṣatriya,
or the body of a Brāhmaṇa, or the body of a Vaiśya, or the body of a Śūdra, or as a male being.
He may manifest in the body of a woman, or the body of a young man, or the body of a young girl,
or the body of a gandharva, or the body of an asura, or the body of a kinnara,
or the body of a mahoraga, or the body of a nāga, or the body of a yakṣa.
Some manifest in the form of rākṣasas, some in the form of kumbhāṇḍas, some in the form of piśācas, some in the form of pretas,
some in the form of putanas, some in the form of kaṭapūtanas,
some in the form of yakṣa-haraloka spirits, some in the form of lions, or some in the form of fragrant beings.
He manifests as the body of an elephant, or the body of a horse, or the body of an ox,
or the bodies of various birds and beasts; or he manifests as the body of King Yama, the Lord of Death, or as the body of a hell-guardian,
or as the bodies of various sentient beings within the hells— manifesting in this way as immeasurable and innumerable bodies of diverse species.
He preaches the Dharma to all sentient beings as appropriate, establishing them, according to their needs,
in the stage of non-retrogression within the three vehicles. "Good son!

Such a Great Being has accomplished such inconceivable dharmas of merit; he is a treasury of these most excellent virtues, a source from which the jewels of liberation emerge, the clear and pure eye of all bodhisattvas, and the guiding leader for merchants journeying toward Nirvāṇa.
In this manner, up until the point where one is able to turn the Great Wheel of Dharma effortlessly, it is as explained extensively before. "Good son!

Suppose there were someone who, for a hundred kalpas, with a sincere heart, took refuge in, invoked the names of, recited the mantras of, prostrated to, made offerings to, and sought all their wishes from Maitreya, Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, Samantabhadra, and others as their leaders—these great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River—it would not equal the merit of someone who, for even the duration of a single meal, with a sincere heart, takes refuge in, invokes the name of, recites the mantra of, prostrates to, and makes offerings to the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, whereby all their wishes will be swiftly fulfilled."

Why is this so? Because Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva benefits and brings peace and happiness to all sentient beings, causing the aspirations of all beings to be fulfilled, like a wish-fulfilling jewel and like a hidden treasure.
Such a Great Being, desiring to bring all sentient beings to maturity, has long cultivated firm great vows, great compassion, valor, and diligence, surpassing all other bodhisattvas.
"Therefore, you all should make offerings.

At that time, the great assembly gathered from the ten directions—all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as well as the śrāvakas, devas, humans, yakṣas, gandharvas, and others—rose from their seats and, according to their respective capacities, each took various kinds of gold and silver powder, as well as various jewels, flowers, and incense, and scattered them over the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha.

Furthermore, they offered various kinds of exquisite garments, mani-jewels, pearl flower-garlands, pearl necklaces, gold and silver precious threads, banners, streamers, and parasols to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha.
Furthermore, they reverently made offerings to the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha with immeasurable, supreme, and exquisite music and various kinds of hymns of praise.
At that time, the Mahāsattva Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha took these various supreme and exquisite offering articles and presented them back to the World-Honored One, speaking in verse:
"Offered by devas, humans, nāgas, and spirits, And brought as tribute by Bodhisattvas from the ten directions."
"Having heard that the Savior possesses great merit, I pray only that you accept my most supreme offering.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, having spoken this verse, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet.
Thereupon the World-Honored One spoke again in verse:
"Arising with firm wisdom and a pure mind, Extinguishing the immeasurable sufferings of all sentient beings;
Bestowing manifold wondrous joys like a precious hand, Able to sever the net of delusions like a vajra."
Arousing great compassion and wisdom, endowed with diligence, Skillfully upholding the sublime offerings to serve the World-Honored One,
With ocean-like intelligence, you rescue suffering sentient beings, And ascend to the fearless shore beyond all realms of existence.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha rose from his seat and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"O Virtuous World-Honored One!
I shall deliver these disciples of the World-Honored One throughout the four continents, as well as all the bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs..."
May bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās all attain these:
the increase of mindfulness, the increase of protective mindfulness, the increase of lifespan, the increase of the physical body,
the increase of freedom from illness, the increase of physical vigor, the increase of renown, and the increase of life’s necessities.
Increasing one's circle of kinsmen and friends; increasing one's disciples; increasing pure ethical discipline;
increasing extensive learning; increasing wisdom and renunciation; increasing sublime meditative concentration; increasing patience; increasing skillful means;
increasing the light of the factors of awakening and the noble truths; increasing the entry into the correct path of the Mahāyāna; and increasing [all these].
The illumination of the Dharma increases; the maturation of sentient beings increases; great loving-kindness and great compassion increase; all wholesome dharmas increase;
the sublime renown that pervades the three realms increases; the rain of Dharma that universally moistens the three realms increases;
the vital essence and flavor of the entire earth increase; and the vitality of all living beings increases.
It causes one to skillfully perform deeds, increases the vital energy of the True Dharma, increases the practice of wholesome conduct, increases the light of wisdom,
increases the sublime practice of the six pāramitās, increases the five eyes, increases empowerment,
and increases rebirth in heaven and nirvāṇa.

This so-called "Possessing the Auspicious Radiance of Water and Fire" Great Dharani-mantra, a dhāraṇī of total retention, was personally received and upheld by me from the World-Honored Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the past. It is capable of increasing all wholesome dharmas; it increases all seeds, roots, fibers, sprouts, stems, branches, leaves, flowers, fruits, medicinal herbs, grains, vital energy, and flavors; it increases rainfall; it increases the beneficial elements of earth, water, fire, and wind; it increases joy and happiness; it increases wealth and treasures; it increases supreme power; and it increases all requisites for enjoyment.
"This dhāraṇī can cause all wisdom to become sharp and keen, and destroy the thieves of affliction.
He then spoke the mantra:
"Excellent teaching that can purify the dust of all existences; Excellent teaching that can purify the kalpa of strife."
Well-spoken words can purify turbid and evil intentions; well-spoken words can purify turbid great elements;
well-spoken words can purify turbid and evil flavors; well-spoken words can purify turbid and evil odors;
well-spoken words can fulfill all hopes and aspirations; well-spoken words can bring all crops and harvests to fruition.
This eloquent exposition causes all Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, the World-Honored Ones, to bestow their protection;
this eloquent exposition also causes all Bodhisattvas to bestow their protection and rejoice in it.
“World-Honored One!

This dharani chapter of the Great Mantra of Auspicious Radiance, which possesses the power over water and fire, I have personally received and upheld from the presence of as many Buddha-Bhagavans as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River in the past.”
"It can cause all wholesome dharmas (*śukladharma*) to increase, and so forth, up to causing all requisites for enjoyment to increase.
'Venerable Blessed One!

This dhāraṇī is universally able to deliver the disciples of the Blessed One throughout these four continents—namely, all bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās—causing them all to attain an increase in mindfulness, and so forth, up to an increase in all requisites for enjoyment.'"
"This dhāraṇī can cause the World-Honored One’s nectar-like holy teaching to blaze forth and endure for a long time, bringing benefit, peace, and happiness to the sentient beings of the three realms.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha expounded such great vidyā-mantra dhāraṇī verses.

At that time, Mount Khadiraka trembled all over; ten billion celestial musical instruments resounded spontaneously without being struck; and immeasurable varieties of exquisite celestial fragrant flowers and rare jewels rained down. The entire assembly was filled with awe and leaped for joy, all attaining something marvelous and unprecedented.

At that time, within the assembly were the goddess Mahāśrī, the goddess Mahāśrīmatī, the goddess Mahāsarasvatī, the goddess Mahādṛḍhā, the goddess Mahātoyavatī, and the goddess Mahāprabhā as their leaders—a total of eighteen thousand goddesses who had attained mastery over the four great elements. They rose from their seats, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, joined their palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“It is rare, O Great Virtuous One!”
"How marvelous, World-Honored One!

Although we have attained mastery over the four great elements, we are unable to know the arising, ceasing, and their mutual opposition or conformity throughout the initial, middle, and final phases of these four great elements."

Such a mahāsattva, having already attained the subtle and profound *prajñāpāramitā*, is able to thoroughly understand the arising, ceasing, and the concordant and discordant characteristics of the beginning, middle, and end of these four great elements.
The Buddha said: “So it is, so it is, O goddess.”

This son of good family has already attained the subtle and profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and is thus able to thoroughly understand the arising and ceasing, as well as the conditions of conformity and opposition, regarding the initial, middle, and final phases of these four great elements.
"O Devī, you should know that just as a wish-fulfilling gem (cintāmaṇi), endowed with all virtues, can rain down various kinds of supreme and wonderful treasures to bestow upon all sentient beings;
so too is this son of good family, who can rain down various kinds of treasures of the factors of enlightenment (bodhipakṣa-dharma) to bestow upon all sentient beings."
Just as a jewel island is filled with all kinds of rare treasures, so too is this son of good family;
he has likewise accomplished the various treasures of the factors of enlightenment.
Just as the celestial pārijātaka tree is adorned with various exquisite fragrant flowers,
so too is this son of good family adorned by the various subtle and wondrous jewels of the Buddha-dharma.
Just as the lion king cannot be startled or subdued by any beast;
so too is this good man, whom no sentient being can startle or subdue.
Just as the bright sun can dispel all the darkness of the world, so too is this son of good family:
he can dispel the darkness of ignorance and all the wrong views of sentient beings.
Just as the bright moon, during the night, can show the level and correct path to all sentient beings who have lost their way, enabling them to reach their destination wherever they wish to go;

so too is this good man: in the night of ignorance, he can show the correct path of the Three Vehicles to all sentient beings who are迷失 (lost) regarding the Three Vehicles and are rushing through the wilderness of birth and death, establishing them through appropriate skillful means according to their needs, so that they may achieve liberation.
Just as the great earth is the support for all seeds, trees, mountains, crops, and the beings who inhabit the land;
so too is this son of good family the support for all the sublime factors of enlightenment.
Just as the Great Jewel King of Mountains, Sumeru, is firmly established, solid, without defect or fissure;
so too is this son of good family, firmly established in all the unique qualities of a Buddha.
Because they do not abandon any sentient beings, it is called "without deficiency.
Because they generously bestow all roots of goodness upon all sentient beings, it is called "without fissure."
Just as all sentient beings rely upon and make use of space, so too is it with this son of good family; all sentient beings rely upon and make use of him.
"This good man has accomplished such immeasurable and boundless dharmas of merit.

At that time, when the great assembly heard it said that the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha had accomplished these immeasurable and praiseworthy merits, they all experienced something rare and unprecedented. With deep respect and reverence, they were filled with great joy and gazed intently upon the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha with their eyes never wavering for a moment.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to further clarify this meaning,
spoke in verse: “The Great Being Kṣitigarbha, Possessing the virtues of dhūta,
Manifests in the form of a śrāvaka, And comes to prostrate before the Great Teacher.”
Bestowing happiness upon all sentient beings, Rescuing them from the suffering of the three realms of existence,
He rained down an immeasurable variety of rains As an offering to the Great Teacher.
The Lord of Devas, Vimala-janman, Having surveyed the four quarters, [proceeded].
Standing with palms joined in reverence, they praised and entreated the Great Teacher:
"I behold the assembly of the World-Honored One; the radiance of mani-jewel gems illuminates all Buddha-lands, leaving nothing unclarified."
With the six supernormal powers illuminating the world, he shall now come here;
named the Valiant Kṣitigarbha, he manifests the majestic deportment of one who has left the household life.
He is the hidden treasury of the seven noble riches and possesses the fearless voice of a Buddha.
The supreme banners of all bodhisattvas, the leaders of sentient beings;
the foundation for the jewel of liberation, possessing an ocean of merit and diligence;
with compassionate intent and keen intelligence, they rescue all suffering sentient beings.
A city for those who fear, showing the way like the bright moon;
Like the earth, it gives rise to roots of goodness; like a diamond, it shatters delusions.
It can bestow the jewel of liberation; like water, it washes away all afflictions.
The heat of afflictions acts as a veil; like a skilled physician, one heals this illness.
To recite the name of Kṣitigarbha for a single day brings forth fame for its vast merit, surpassing the praise of other wise ones throughout ten million kalpas.
Able to liberate all sentient beings from the bonds of all afflictions,
reaching the perfection of the "Heroic Progression" (*vīryapāramitā*) and other meditative concentrations;
with the twelve links of dependent origination purified, their various wisdoms are like space.
Shattering boundless buddha-fields and the masses of darkness for all sentient beings,
they enter meditative absorption in accordance with each field; through the natural outflow of the four dhyānas,
they cause all sentient beings everywhere to enter absorption and eliminate the fever of their afflictions.
The evil karma of sentient beings from past lives— Armed conflict, disease, and famine—
Whatever afflictions and harms they encounter wherever they may be, All can be made to attain liberation.
The bodies of sentient beings within the five destinies, Pressed and tormented by all manner of sufferings,
Those who take refuge in and revere Kṣitigarbha have all their sufferings completely eliminated.
Sentient beings ride upon the wheel of suffering, revolving in mutual conflict and harm;
those who take refuge in and revere Kṣitigarbha all abide in a mind of patience and compassion.
Those who fear the twelve links of dependent origination, the basis of suffering sought through craving, take refuge in and revere Kṣitigarbha; they shall all abide in fearlessness.
If one delights in cultivating various merits, maintaining right mindfulness of precepts, learning, and wisdom, [one shall likewise attain this].
Those who take refuge and pay homage to Kṣitigarbha shall have all their requests fulfilled.
Those who delight in each of his merits— whether in craftsmanship, medicine, or seeds—
and take refuge and pay homage to Kṣitigarbha, shall have all their requests fulfilled.
Those who seek various grains, medicines, fields, sons, daughters, clothing, and servants,
and who take refuge in and revere Kṣitigarbha, shall have all their requests fulfilled.
Endowed with all virtues, he is able to sustain the great earth.
Because of these various grains and medicinal herbs, they become moist, lustrous, and soft.
Those covered by various afflictions who delight in practicing the ten unwholesome deeds—
by taking refuge in and honoring Kṣitigarbha, all their afflictions and evils are eliminated.
Manifesting in various forms, he preaches the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings;
fully endowed with the merit of giving, he feels compassion for all living beings.
Even if one were to praise his merits throughout a hundred kalpas, [they would not be exhausted].
Even this would not suffice; therefore, all should offer worship. The Mahāyāna Mahāsannipāta Kṣitigarbha Daśacakra Sūtra, Scroll One.
Translated by the Dharma Master Xuanzang by imperial decree at the Translation Hall of the Great Ci’en Monastery on the twenty-third day of the first month in the second year of the Yonghui era.

Chapter Two: The Ten Wheels.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, bared one shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I now question the World-Honored One, the ocean of immeasurable merit;
I only pray that you will grant me leave to explain and dispel my doubts.
The World-Honored One replied:
“You are a true and virtuous person!
Your knowledge and vision regarding all phenomena are unimpeded; it is because you wish to benefit other sentient beings that you have questioned the Tathāgata.
Ask whatever you desire, and I shall analyze and explain it for you, so as to bring joy to your heart.”
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha asked in verse:
“For thirteen kalpas past, I have already diligently practiced asceticism For the sake of all sentient beings,
To eliminate the three calamities and the five turbidities.”
At the abodes of many koṭis of Buddhas, they have already offered boundless offerings;
they have witnessed great assemblies where the pure-faithed congregations were in harmony;
the wise and diligent, all having applied themselves with vigor, have come together to gather in this assembly.
Never before have I seen such a place, Devoid of all manner of impurities and defilements.
How is it that this Buddha-land Is so foul and corrupt, diminishing pure goodness?
The wise all distance themselves from it, Yet those of evil conduct dwell together therein.

Having committed many crimes of immediate retribution, slandering the True Dharma, disparaging the Noble Ones, and giving rise to evil views; falsely propounding theories of annihilationism or eternalism;
fully committing the ten unwholesome karmas, they fear not the suffering of future lives.
Most have abandoned the Three Vehicles; foul and defiled, they head toward evil realms.
Ignorance blinds their eyes, and greed and envy abound with deceit and hypocrisy.
How can you turn the Buddha’s wheel and deliver these classes of sentient beings?
How does one shatter the continuity of afflictions as hard as a vajra?
How does one attain dhāraṇī, such that the fruit is able to endure thus?
Now I behold the Teacher; this great assembly is most rare.
I have never seen elsewhere such a multitude of virtues as these:
possessing the qualities of the dhūtas and diligently cultivating the path to enlightenment.
How is it that, dwelling among the ignorant masses, you are able to reveal the Buddha’s wheel?
The World-Honored One said:
"Excellent, excellent! O son of good family!"

In the past, throughout Buddha-worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, during the degenerate times of the five turbidities, you have already inquired about such meanings of the Dharma from Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Regarding the meaning of the Dharma thus questioned, you have already exerted diligent effort, have already attained thorough mastery, and have reached the further shore of all perfected practices;
you have already acquired skillful means and sublime wisdom.
It is now for the sake of bringing all sentient beings to maturity so that they may attain benefit and happiness;

for the sake of causing all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to swiftly fulfill the great ocean of merit—the supreme practice of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*)—by means of skillful means, noble conduct, hidden treasures, and the six perfections such as giving, thereby maturing all sentient beings;
and for the sake of transforming the violent and evil deeds of all kṣatriya kings so that they do not fall into the three miserable realms.
In order that the lineage of the Triple Gem in this land may flourish with majestic power and endure for a long time in the world,
he again questioned the Tathāgata regarding such principles of the Dharma.
Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon them well!
"I shall analyze and explain this for you. "Indeed,
World-Honored One!"
"I wish to hear it with joy.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, saying:
"O son of good family!"
By the power of his original vows, the Tathāgata has accomplished ten kinds of Buddha-wheels.

All sentient beings dwelling in this Buddha-land of the five turbidities and evil world have fallen away from all pure and wholesome dharmas; they are destitute of all the seven treasures of the noble ones; they are far removed from all the wise and sagacious; and they are shrouded by the net of the views of annihilation and permanence.
They constantly delight in riding the chariots of the various evil destinies and feel no dread toward the sufferings of future lives.

They constantly dwell in the pervasive and heavy darkness of ignorance, fully possessing the ten unwholesome paths of action, committing the five deeds of immediate retribution, slandering the true Dharma, reviling the noble ones, abandoning all wholesome dharmas, and being endowed with all unwholesome dharmas.
Dwelling within such a defiled and evil land, I abide in peace, free from alarm and fear.

I declare that I occupy the exalted position of a Great Sage, turning the Wheel of the Buddha, subduing all devas, Māras, and non-Buddhist heretics with their fallacious doctrines, and crushing the afflictions of all classes of sentient beings as if they were adamantine and solid. According to their inclinations, I establish all capable sentient beings in the stage of non-retrogression within the Three Vehicles.

“Good son! It is like a kingdom where the throne is vacant for a time; all the people therein, as well as their own armies and those of other nations, mutually inflict harm upon one another, becoming distressed and agitated, so that the masses live in insecurity.”
There are immeasurable kinds of strife, litigation, and disputes; mutual bullying; flattery, falsehood, harsh speech, divisiveness, slander, and deceitful confusion;
various diseases such as cataracts and blindness, feverish delirium, chills and fevers, malaria, contagious epidemics, epilepsy, emaciation, and indigestion;
their minds are deranged and their faculties incomplete; their limbs are deficient; they lack various necessities of food, clothing, and utensils; and everything they possess is utterly unpleasant.

All classes of sentient beings take refuge in various external paths and false deities; their evil views, malicious minds, and corrupt inclinations are all intensely blazing, causing them to lose the right path and stand on the verge of falling into the miserable realms.

At that time, there were several elders in that kingdom who were intelligent, wise, erudite, impartial and forgiving, majestic, and dignified. They consulted together and devised various strategies, immediately summoning the people of the kingdom and its towns to collectively select and recommend one prince.
Previously, he had fully perfected all manner of manifold practices: generosity, self-mastery, tranquility, ethical discipline, diligence, valor, difficult feats, and ascetic austerities.

He was endowed with all the marks of excellent merit; his faculties were complete, his limbs were without deficiency, his body was tall and large, his features were dignified and handsome, and he possessed a most supreme and beautiful complexion.

He was always respected and honored by all; throughout the land, there were none among the people who did not hold him in affection. By nature he was pure and sincere, constantly harboring compassion and kindness; he was widely learned and possessed many talents, being fully equipped with all arts and skills.
Gentle and patient, he adorns his mind.
As the legitimate son born of the Great Queen, his body is bathed with pure water scented with various exquisite fragrances, tempered to a balanced temperature.

He was adorned with various exquisite perfumes, many jewels, ornaments, and fresh, pure garments; mani-jewels were placed within his topknot, a crown of golden jewel-flower garlands graced his head, and fine white silk was bound at the hairline.

Furthermore, his body was adorned with various exquisite jewel ornaments—such as earrings, necklaces, bracelets, and seals—all fashioned from a combination of diverse mani-jewels, pearls, gold, silver, and other precious gems.

Woven precious sandals were placed beneath his feet to support them, and a parasol made of various jewels was held over his head; he was then seated upon a throne protected by all the celestial sages of antiquity.
He entered the exquisite great palace, skillfully constructed and protected by the consensus of all the celestial lords, and ascended the noble throne upon which his own ancestors had previously sat.

Having ascended the throne as king, he struck all the great bells and drums protected by the various lords of the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, divine beings, asuras, and kumbhāṇḍas; their resounding vibrations pervaded the entire realm.

"Countless people from the four great castes, such as the Kṣatriyas, having bathed their bodies and donned clean garments, held various exquisite jewels, silken banners, parasols, pennants, mani-gems, pearls, gold, silver, conch shells, jade, coral, lapis lazuli, and other dyed precious materials of infinite rarity, and offered them to the new king to present as auspicious omens."

The noble, pure-living, and highly learned Brahmins, with immeasurable kinds of subtle praises and hymns, extolled the Emperor’s virtues; they offered various auspicious benedictions for the King and scattered all manner of auspicious substances over his head.

Those esteemed by the former kings—noble clans of long-standing reputation who were erudite and possessed many arts, upright by nature and wise—were granted various positions, offices, and bureaucratic roles according to their respective merits to manage the affairs of the kingdom.
First, let the mutual injuries inflicted by our own armies and those of others upon the borders of the kingdom now all cease.
Furthermore, let all enemies, evil associates, and those capable of causing harm be utterly extinguished.
He eliminates all unwholesome factors within his own realm and increases all wholesome factors within his own realm.
Son of good family!
A consecrated Great King of the Kṣatriya caste achieves such a foremost royal wheel.
By means of this wheel, one attains peaceful dwelling within one's own realm, is able to subdue all enemies and evil associates, well protects the body, and causes the lifespan to increase.

“Good son! In this defiled world of the five turbidities, the Sahā Buddha-field, when it is empty and devoid of a Buddha, all sentient beings therein are afflicted by the latent tendencies, fetters, and impurities within their own minds. Oppressed and harassed by their own armies and those of others, they are distressed, agitated, and bewildered by ignorance. They give rise to immeasurable varieties of attachment to the views of annihilationism and eternalism, engage in strife, litigation, and contention, and mutually despise one another. They give rise to greed, hatred, delusion, flattery, and deceitful speech, fully possessing the ten paths of unwholesome action.”

Attached to the turbulent world of sentient beings, they give rise to various afflictions and diseases; lacking the eye of the True Dharma, they are consumed by anger and resentment. They never contemplate the true, authentic Dharma, abandon the flavor of the True Dharma, and revile virtuous conduct. Deprived of the taste of joy and bliss, they are constantly shrouded by the nets of various afflictions. Taking refuge in the six kinds of heterodox teachers, they lose their way on the Noble Path and head toward the three evil realms.

"In this land, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have already in the past approached and made offerings to immeasurable buddhas; who have already entered the great ocean of the buddhas' merits; and who have already dwelled in the path originally practiced by the buddhas. They have all gathered together and come to my place, speaking to me in unison:

'In the past, you have already cultivated immeasurable generosity, self-discipline, tranquility, ethical conduct (*śīla*), diligence, and valor; all difficult practices and ascetic austerities have been fully perfected.'"

This is a treasury of great merit, exquisitely adorned by all manner of subtle qualities—merit, wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion; it is a vast ocean that perfectly fulfills all concentrations, dhāraṇīs, patient endurance, and the virtues of the stages, free from guile and deceit.
His physical form was tall and large, his marks and signs were perfectly complete, he was patient and gentle, and he was upright and most exquisite.
No longer relying on others to cultivate the path to enlightenment, he had already attained perfection in the ocean of all-knowledge and achieved a most supreme and beautiful countenance.
He is able to act as a great guide for all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
