"Furthermore, noble son!

If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others do not cling to this world, this is called the sixth dharma, which enables bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others to attain the patient acceptance of the dharma of the faultless, correct path."
"Furthermore, son of good family!

If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others do not cling to future lives, this is called the seventh dharma, which enables bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others to attain the patient acceptance (*kṣānti*) of the faultless path of the Dharma."
"Furthermore, son of good family!

If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others do not cling to the desire realm, this is called the eighth dharma, which enables bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others to attain the dharma-patience of the faultless right path."
"Furthermore, noble son!

If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others do not cling to the form realm, this is called the ninth dharma, which enables bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others to attain the patient acceptance of the Dharma regarding the faultless, correct path."
"Furthermore, noble son!

If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others do not cling to the formless realm, this is called the tenth dharma, which enables bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others to attain the patient acceptance of the faultless path of Dharma."
“O sons of good family!
These are called the ten dharmas that enable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others to attain the dharma-patience of the faultless, correct path.

When the World-Honored One preached this Dharma for the assembly, seventy-two hundred thousand koṭis of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas within the gathering simultaneously realized the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
Furthermore, there were eighty-four hundred thousand nayutas of bodhisattvas who attained the patient acceptance that accords with the Dharma (anulomikī-dharmakṣānti).
Additionally, there were immeasurable hundreds of thousands of śrāvakas who, having forever severed all afflictions, became arhats.

Furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of nayutas of sentient beings who had not previously resolved their minds [on enlightenment], but now gave rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, and came to abide in the stage of non-retrogression regarding the wisdom of the Tathāgata.

Furthermore, there were immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings who had not previously resolved their minds [for enlightenment], but now for the first time resolved their minds toward the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddhas.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings who had not previously resolved their minds, but now for the first time resolved their minds toward the vehicle of the Śrāvakas.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the great assembly:

"If there are sentient beings who have already attained the patience of the Dharma (*dharmakṣānti*), and occupy the consecrated royal throne of a Kṣatriya, enjoying various kinds of excellent wealth and undertakings, as well as various positions of prosperity and honor—it is for these that I grant permission, and not for other sentient beings."
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If there are sentient beings who have not yet attained the patience of the Dharma (*dharmakṣānti*), would it be definitively impermissible for them to occupy the consecrated royal throne of a Kṣatriya, or to enjoy various kinds of superior wealth and undertakings, as well as other various forms of prosperity, nobility, and high status?”
"Is this also permitted? The World-Honored One replied, "If there are sentient beings who,

though they have not yet attained the patience of the Dharma (*dharmakṣānti*), are able to receive and practice the ten paths of wholesome action (*daśakuśalakarmapatha*) and also encourage other beings to receive and study them, I likewise permit them to occupy the consecrated kṣatriya royal throne, enjoy various kinds of excellent and great wealth and undertakings, as well as other various forms of prosperity, nobility, and high status."

If there are sentient beings who have not yet attained the patient acceptance of the Dharma (*dharmakṣānti*), nor practice the ten paths of wholesome action themselves, nor exhort others to diligently study them, yet by means of their powerful influence occupy the consecrated royal throne of a Kṣatriya, enjoying various kinds of superior wealth and undertakings, as well as various kinds of wealthy, noble, and honorable positions—such a person is called a "Kṣatriya Caṇḍāla king," as well as a "Caṇḍāla king" in other various kinds of wealthy, noble, and honorable positions.
They will be foolish, arrogant, destructive, and disruptive toward my profound Dharma; they will extinguish the lamp of the True Dharma and sever the seeds of the Triple Gem.

Toward those disciples who have gone forth under me, they will cause various forms of harassment and disturbance, subjecting them to beatings and punishments, confiscating their robes, bowls, livelihoods, and property, forcing them to return to lay life, imposing taxes and corvée labor, imprisoning them in jails, and even depriving them of their lives.
They will slander, despise, obstruct, and conceal the subtle Dharma and its meaning as I have taught them, preventing their dissemination; they will seize stūpas and the property of the Saṃgha.
"All such persons as these shall surely fall into the Avīci Hell, where they will undergo various intense sufferings and revolve through the evil destinies, with no foreseeable time of escape.
At that time, Vajragarbha Bodhisattva again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If there are sentient beings who have not yet attained the patient acceptance of the Dharma (*dharmakṣānti*), nor practice the ten paths of wholesome action, nor exhort other beings to diligently study them, yet by means of forceful power occupy the position of a consecrated Kṣatriya king, enjoying various kinds of superior and great wealth and activities, as well as other various forms of opulence and honorable status.

"Is there perhaps some other cause by which a skillful means could be found to rescue them, so that they might avoid falling into the Avīci Hell and the other evil destinies where they would undergo various sufferings?
The World-Honored One replied,
"There is indeed another cause by which a skillful means may be found to rescue them."

It refers to sentient beings who occupy the position of a consecrated Kṣatriya king or other various positions of wealth, honor, and nobility; although they have not yet attained the perfection of the patience of dharmas (dharmakṣānti) or the ten paths of wholesome action, they possess the power of faith and revere the Triple Gem. Regarding the various methods of deliverance associated with the Three Vehicles taught by the Buddha, even down to a single verse, they never slander, obstruct, conceal, or prevent them from being spread.

Regarding the assembly of disciples who have gone forth under the Buddha—whether they maintain the precepts, violate them, or even lack them entirely, provided they have shaved their hair and beards and donned the *kāṣāya*—one shall not disturb, beat, torture, or punish them; nor shall one seize their robes, bowls, dwellings, foundations, or property; nor cause them to return to lay life, subject them to taxes or forced labor, imprison them, or even deprive them of life. Furthermore, one shall not seize the property of *stūpas* or the communal property of the Saṃgha. One shall restrain and subdue all violent and wicked persons so as not to disturb the ordained community, and not allow them to plunder the wealth and goods of the Triple Gem.

Regarding the various methods for transcendence corresponding to the three vehicles taught by the Buddha, they listen to and receive them with reverence; having listened and received them, they practice with diligence, conducting themselves in accordance with the Dharma.
They reverently make offerings to, draw near to, and serve my noble disciples of the three vehicles;

within the Mahāyāna, their vows are firm, and they never harbor a mind of doubt, difficulty, or retreat; furthermore, they constantly exhort and establish sentient beings, causing them to believe in, accept, and practice the Mahāyāna.

These kṣatriya caṇḍāla kings, as well as other various wealthy and noble caṇḍāla kings, have all been permitted by the Buddhas of the past to occupy the position of sovereign and other various positions of wealth and nobility.
Although they may enjoy various kingdoms, cities, villages, and vast wealth and enterprises, they shall avoid falling into the Avīci Hell or other evil destinies.

I also grant permission that, while occupying the position of a sovereign or other various ranks of wealth and honor, and though one may enjoy various kingdoms, cities, and villages, one shall nevertheless avoid falling into the Avīci Hell or the other evil destinies.

“If there are sentient beings who wish to repent and eliminate all karmic obstructions without exception, they should diligently practice and study this Dharma gate as taught by me, and not allow it to be neglected or forgotten.”

If there are those who, before this present great assembly, feel shame and remorse and repent for their various evil deeds, all the evil karma created in previous lives shall be completely extinguished without remainder.
The Mahāyāna Mahāsannipāta Kṣitigarbha Daśacakra Sūtra, Scroll Seven;
The Mahāyāna Mahāsannipāta Kṣitigarbha Daśacakra Sūtra, Scroll Eight.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Six: On the Paths of Wholesome Action, Part One.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajragarbha again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"O Virtuous World-Honored One!"
How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva avoid error regarding the Śrāvaka vehicle?
How does he avoid error regarding the individuals (pudgala) of the Śrāvaka vehicle?
How does one attain freedom from error regarding the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle?
How does one attain freedom from error regarding individuals belonging to the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle?
How does one attain freedom from error regarding the Mahāyāna?
How does one avoid error regarding persons belonging to the Mahāyāna?
How does one always cause the lineage of the Three Jewels to blaze forth?

And how does one avoid error regarding all the ordained disciples of the Tathāgatas—whether they be vessels of the Dharma or not vessels of the Dharma—even down to those who have merely donned a fragment of the saffron robe and shaved their hair and beards?
How may one always advance in the Mahāyāna teachings without ever regressing?
How may one’s sharp wisdom and supreme merit constantly increase?
How may one swiftly attain mastery over all meditative concentrations, dhāraṇīs, patiences, and stages, without ever regressing?
How can one always encounter all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) and act in accordance with them?

How can one always never be separated from seeing all Buddhas, as well as bodhisattvas and śrāvaka disciples; never be separated from hearing the Dharma; and never be separated from attending upon and making offerings to the Saṃgha?
How does one constantly and diligently seek all roots of goodness with a mind that never knows satiety?
How does one constantly [seek] the various practices and vows for enlightenment with a mind that never knows satiety?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajragarbha, saying: “Good son!
There are ten wheels of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva. If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva accomplishes these ten wheels, they will attain freedom from error regarding the Śrāvaka Vehicle.”
He attains freedom from error regarding persons of the Śrāvaka vehicle;
he attains freedom from error regarding the Pratyekabuddha vehicle;
and he attains freedom from error regarding persons of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle.
They attain freedom from error regarding the Mahāyāna;
they attain freedom from error regarding individuals within the Mahāyāna;
and they are always able to cause the lineage of the Three Jewels to blaze forth.

Regarding all disciples who have gone forth under the Tathāgatas—whether they be vessels of the Dharma or not, down to those who merely wear a fragment of the *kāṣāya* robe and have shaved their hair and beards—one shall never err or fail;
one shall always advance in the Mahāyāna Dharma without ever regressing;
and one’s sharp wisdom and supreme merit shall constantly increase.
They will swiftly attain mastery over all meditative concentrations, dhāraṇīs, patiences, and stages, remaining irreversible;
they will constantly encounter spiritual friends and act in accordance with their guidance;
and they will never be separated from seeing all Buddhas, nor from bodhisattvas and śrāvaka disciples, nor from hearing the Dharma, nor from attending upon and making offerings to the Saṅgha.
One constantly and diligently seeks all roots of goodness, with a mind that never knows satiety;
one constantly pursues the various practices and vows for enlightenment, with a mind that never knows satiety;

and regarding all previously committed evil and unwholesome karma, one uses the noble, adamantine, firm, and sharp wisdom of the Dharma to shatter, destroy, and disperse them, leaving nothing remaining so that no karmic retribution is experienced.
They shall no longer create new evil or unwholesome karma; with minds free from weariness, they will swiftly realize the unsurpassed Wheel of Dharma.
They shall constantly and diligently cultivate the jewels of the seven factors of enlightenment, their minds never wearying.
He is always able to eliminate the diseases of affliction of all sentient beings, his mind never weary;
all sentient beings rely upon him for their survival. "Good son!

Just as a wheel-turning monarch, endowed with the seven treasures, wherever he moves, has the wheel-treasure lead the way and the other treasures follow behind, as he tours the four great continents, universally able to eliminate all turbidity and impurity of body and mind for all sentient beings, and universally able to produce and increase all peace and happiness of body and mind for all sentient beings.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is likewise; having accomplished the ten wheels, he incurs no error regarding the Śrāvaka vehicle, and so on extensively until: all sentient beings rely upon him for their subsistence.

“Good son! It is like a great carriage equipped with four wheels, which many people ride upon as they travel along a great road. On that road, clods of earth, shards, pebbles, grasses, trees, roots, stalks, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits are all crushed by the wheels; they are utterly destroyed and no longer fit for use.”

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: by accomplishing the ten wheels, they are able to utterly destroy all obstructions of afflictions, obstructions of sentient beings, and obstructions regarding all phenomena, ensuring that these do not result in karmic retribution.
“Good son! Just as a sharp wheel of swords, upon being cast but once, can sever the heads and limbs of enemies, rendering them powerless, so too is it with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.

Having accomplished the ten wheels, he is able to shatter all the prisons of the five destinies and the great suffering of birth and death; he forever cuts off all afflictions and evil karma, ensuring that they do not receive retribution.”
“Good son! Just as when the calamity of fire arises and five suns appear, all rivers, seas, and watery realms throughout the four great continents will dry up completely, leaving nothing behind.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: by accomplishing the ten wheels, all four causes—the afflictive obscurations, the obscurations of sentient beings, and the fundamental roots of the retributive suffering of all dharma-obscuring factors—are entirely dried up.

“Good son! Just as when a wind calamity arises, fierce winds from the four directions suddenly break forth all at once, causing all the great and small mountains and the vast earth of every world-system to be utterly dispersed and destroyed.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: having accomplished the ten wheels, there are none of the four inversions of the world or the mountains of pride that do not collapse; all the affliction-obstructions, sentient-being-obstructions, and dharma-obstructions of all beings—the very roots of the retribution of suffering—are entirely dispersed and extinguished.
“Good son! Just as when the lion king lets out a single roar, all birds and beasts are utterly terrified; they either fall from flight or crouch to hide, none daring to move at will.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is likewise; having accomplished the ten wheels, with a single resonance of the Dharma-sound, all those who follow external paths, heterodox teachings, and evil associates are utterly struck with terror. They lose their eloquence and speech, and none dare to respond or oppose him.

“Good son! It is like when Śakra, Lord of the Devas, is about to go to war with the asuras; surrounded by the celestial armies and grasping a vajra in his hand, he rushes toward the enemy ranks, and all the asuras are struck with terror and retreat in dispersal.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: having accomplished the ten wheels, all those with inverted views—non-Buddhists, heterodox practitioners, and evil associates—are struck with terror and disperse.
“Good son! Just as when a wish-fulfilling jewel is placed atop a high banner, it can rain down all kinds of exquisite and precious treasures to provide for all impoverished sentient beings.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: having accomplished the ten wheels and standing upon the banner of pure precepts, he rains down the great Dharma rain, bestowing it upon all immeasurable sentient beings.
“Good son! Just as during the hours of darkness, the world is shrouded in gloom and nothing can be seen, causing those who have lost their way to wander;
once the full moon has risen, all darkness is dispelled, and all who were lost see the correct path.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is likewise; having accomplished the ten wheels, when sentient beings are shrouded in the darkness of ignorance and thereby lose their way on the Noble Eightfold Path, the Bodhisattva proclaims the True Dharma for them. He dispels the darkness of ignorance and gives rise to the light of the Dharma, revealing and manifesting the Noble Eightfold Path, so that they may sever all outflows and reach the end of all suffering.

“Good son! Just as when the palace of Mahāvairocana appears in the world, all crops and vegetation flourish and grow; all flowers and leaves bloom and flourish; all foul odors and impurities are entirely eliminated; all grains, fruits, and medicinal herbs reach full maturity; the snow mountains melt and flow, causing the various rivers to overflow; and as they gradually pour into one another, they fill the great ocean.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: having accomplished the ten wheels and relying upon superior generosity, self-discipline, tranquility, ethical conduct (*śīla*), patience, right effort, meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), and wisdom (*prajñā*), their skillful means, compassion, eloquence, and meritorious qualities all blaze forth. For the sake of all sentient beings, they proclaim the True Dharma; by the majestic light of that Dharma, they cause the various crops of the superior roots of goodness of all sentient beings to grow;
the various flowers and leaves of superior sublime practices to flourish and bloom;
and all various afflictions, evil karma, and unwholesome deeds to be extinguished.
The grains, fruits, and medicinal herbs of the happy realms and nirvana all reach full maturity;
the mountains of wrong views and pride are entirely dissolved and dispersed;
and the various rivers of right faith, precepts, learning, renunciation, wisdom, and meditative concentration overflow without exception, gradually filling the great ocean of nirvana.
"May all sentient beings, according to their inclinations and desires, enter the city of fearless nirvāṇa. "Good son,
what are called the ten wheels of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva?"
"Good son! These ten wheels are not some other dharma; you should know that they are precisely the ten paths of wholesome action.
Because one accomplishes these ten kinds of wheels, one receives the name 'Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.'"
One is able to be liberated from all evils, accomplishes all wholesome dharmas according to one's will, and can swiftly fill the great ocean of *nirvāṇa*.
By means of the light of wisdom of great skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), one brings all classes of sentient beings to maturity, causing them all to obtain benefit and peace.
Why is this so? Good son!

All the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past were entirely free from the ten paths of unwholesome action, and they all extolled and praised the fruits and rewards obtained through these ten paths of wholesome action.

Therefore, if one can protect even a single one of these ten paths of wholesome action as they have been explained, and remain ultimately free from transgression until the end of life, one will certainly obtain all the most excellent fruits and rewards as previously described.
“Good son! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can, for as long as life lasts, remain far removed from taking life, he thereby bestows upon all sentient beings freedom from alarm and fear.”
May all sentient beings not give rise to sorrow or suffering, and be freed from the fear that makes one's hair stand on end.
By this, their roots of goodness will quickly reach maturity.

Whatever obstacles of physical, verbal, and mental karma, obstacles of afflictions, obstacles of sentient beings, obstacles of all phenomena, and obstacles of lifespan they have created throughout the past while wandering through the five destinies and sinking in the river of birth and death—due to killing; whether committed by themselves, incited in others, or rejoiced in upon seeing or hearing [others do so]—all these shall be completely ground down, crushed, and extinguished without remainder by virtue of turning away from the wheel of killing, such that no karmic retribution shall be experienced.
In this very life, all humans, devas, and others will hold them in common affection;
free from suspicion or anxiety, their bodies and minds will be peaceful and joyful, and their lifespan will be long.
At the time of death, his body and mind will not be oppressed by grief or suffering, and he will be surrounded by his beloved wife, children, and kinsmen.
As he approaches the end of life, he will not see the terrifying messengers of King Yama;
instead, he will see only those who have mastered the well-disciplined Dharma, who possess the precepts and abundant virtue—true fields of merit—as his spiritual friends.
With body and mind filled with joy, they develop deep reverence and faith.

After their lives come to an end, they are reborn among humans; their sense faculties are complete, their limbs are fully formed, and wherever they are born, they are free from illness, long-lived, handsome, intelligent, and live in peace and happiness.
Furthermore, they encounter a spiritual friend who is pleasing to the mind, one who has mastered the well-disciplined Dharma, is endowed with precepts, rich in virtue, and is a true field of merit.

Relying upon them, they train in the practice of abstaining from taking life; they are able to sever all evil and unwholesome dharmas, accomplish all sublime wholesome dharmas, seek the meaning of all Mahāyāna teachings, and cultivate all the vows and practices of a bodhisattva. Thus, they gradually enter the deep and vast ocean of wisdom, until finally attaining unsurpassed bodhi.

The Buddha-land where he dwells is free from all weapons; even the names of enmity, harm, and combat do not exist there. All fears are severed, and it is peaceful, secure, and blissful; all long-lived sentient beings who are free from illness come to be born in that land.
The Tathāgata’s own lifespan is immeasurable and boundless, and he teaches the Dharma to all sentient beings according to their needs.
After his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain for a long time, bringing benefit and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings.
“Good son! This is called the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s first wheel of complete distancing from taking life.
Because the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva accomplishes this wheel, he attains freedom from error regarding the Śrāvaka Vehicle.”
He is free from error regarding persons of the Śrāvaka vehicle;
he is free from error regarding the Pratyekabuddha vehicle;
and he is free from error regarding persons of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle.
They attain freedom from error regarding the Mahāyāna;
they attain freedom from error regarding individuals within the Mahāyāna;
and they are always able to cause the lineage of the Three Jewels to blaze forth.

Regarding all disciples who have gone forth under the Tathāgatas—whether they be vessels of the Dharma or not, down to anyone who has donned even a fragment of the saṃghāṭī robe and shaved their hair and beard—one must never commit an error or offense against them.
Within the Mahāyāna teachings, they shall constantly attain advancement without ever regressing;
their sharp wisdom and superior merit shall always increase;
and regarding all meditative concentrations, dhāraṇīs, patiences, and stages, they shall swiftly attain mastery without ever regressing.
They constantly encounter various spiritual friends and act in accordance with them;
they never fail to see all Buddhas, nor to be with Bodhisattvas and Śrāvaka disciples; they never cease hearing the Dharma, nor ceasing to approach and make offerings to the Sangha;
they always seek out roots of goodness with diligent effort, their minds never knowing satiety.
He is always insatiable in his mind regarding the various practices and vows for enlightenment.
The resulting rewards he attains are as extensively described previously. "Furthermore, good son!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to refrain from taking what is not given for as long as their life lasts, they thereby bestow upon all sentient beings freedom from alarm, fear, feverish affliction, and agitation.
Regarding the Dharma-conformable wealth and benefits one has obtained, one dwells in contentment and never seeks after wealth or benefits that are contrary to the Dharma.
By this means, one's roots of goodness quickly reach maturity.

All those who, throughout the beginningless cycle of transmigration within the five destinies and submerged in the river of birth and death, have—due to taking what is not given—created various obstacles of bodily, verbal, and mental unwholesome karma; obstacles of afflictions, obstacles regarding sentient beings, obstacles regarding all phenomena, and obstacles regarding material wealth; whether committed by oneself, incited in others, or rejoiced in upon seeing or hearing them performed—all such things are completely ground down, crushed, and extinguished without remainder by this wheel of abstaining from taking what is not given, so that no karmic retribution is experienced.

In this very life, all humans, devas, and others will hold them in common affection and harbor no suspicion; their bodies and minds will be peaceful and happy, and they will be fully endowed with wealth and treasures.
At the time of death, his body and mind will not be oppressed by sorrow or suffering, and he will be surrounded by his beloved wife, children, and kinsmen.
As he approaches the end of life, he will not see the terrifying messengers of King Yama;

instead, he will see only those who are pleasing to him—those who have perfected the well-disciplined Dharma, are endowed with precepts, are rich in virtue, and are true fields of merit, serving as his spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra).
With body and mind filled with joy, they develop deep reverence and faith.

After their lives have ended, they are reborn among human beings, with all faculties complete and limbs fully formed. Wherever they are born, they possess great wealth and treasures; they are handsome and intelligent, living in peace and happiness, and their riches are not shared with the "five families" who consume them.
Furthermore, they encounter a spiritual friend who is pleasing to the mind, one who has perfected the well-disciplined Dharma, is endowed with precepts, rich in virtue, and is a true field of merit.

Relying upon them for study and practice, they abandon taking what is not given; they are able to sever all evil and unwholesome dharmas, accomplish all sublime wholesome dharmas, seek the meaning of all Mahāyāna teachings, and cultivate all the vows and practices of a bodhisattva. Thus, they gradually enter the deep and vast ocean of wisdom, until finally attaining unsurpassed bodhi.
The buddha-field where he dwells is adorned with various jewels; there is nothing lacking among its jewel trees, jewel ponds, and jewel palaces and halls.
Free from the notions of "I" and "mine," and without anything to be grasped, it is fully endowed with all manner of magnificent ornaments, and sentient beings come to be born in that land.

The Tathāgata’s own lifespan is immeasurable; he teaches the Dharma to all sentient beings as is appropriate for them, and after his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall abide for a long time, bringing benefit and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings.
"Good son! This is called the second wheel of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva for remaining far removed from taking what is not given.
Because the bodhisattva-mahāsattva accomplishes this wheel, he attains freedom from error regarding the Śrāvaka Vehicle."
He attains freedom from error regarding individuals of the Śrāvaka vehicle;
he attains freedom from error regarding the Pratyekabuddha vehicle;
and he attains freedom from error regarding individuals of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle.
They attain freedom from error regarding the Mahāyāna;
they attain freedom from error regarding individuals within the Mahāyāna;
and they are always able to cause the lineage of the Triple Gem to blaze forth.

Regarding the ordained disciples of all Tathāgatas—whether they be vessels of the Dharma or not vessels of the Dharma, down to those who have merely donned a fragment of the kāṣāya and shaved their hair and beards—one must never commit an error or offense against them.
They shall always attain advancement in the Mahāyāna teachings without ever regressing;
their sharp wisdom and supreme merit shall constantly increase;
and they shall swiftly attain mastery over all meditative concentrations, dhāraṇīs, patiences, and stages, never falling back.
They always encounter various spiritual friends and act in accordance with them;
they never fail to see all Buddhas, nor to be with Bodhisattvas and Śrāvaka disciples; they never cease hearing the Dharma, nor ceasing to approach and make offerings to the Sangha;
regarding all roots of goodness, they always seek them with diligent effort, their minds never knowing satiety.
He is always insatiable in his mind regarding the various practices and vows for enlightenment.
The resulting retributions he attains are as extensively described above. "Furthermore, good son!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to refrain from sexual misconduct for as long as they live, they bestow upon all sentient beings drifting in the stream of desire a state free from alarm, fear, envy, and harm, and one devoid of feverish affliction or agitation.
Content with his own wife, he never seeks improper sensual desires.
By this means, his roots of virtue quickly reach maturity.

All the obstacles of body, speech, and mind, the obstacles of afflictions, the obstacles of sentient beings, the obstacles to all dharmas, and the obstacles of domestic life—which he created through sexual misconduct while wandering through the five destinies and sinking in the river of birth and death since beginningless time—whether committed by himself, incited in others, or rejoiced in upon seeing or hearing them, are all completely crushed, destroyed, and extinguished without remainder by turning away from the wheel of sexual misconduct; thus, he shall not undergo their karmic retribution.

In this present life, all humans, devas, and others will hold them in common affection and harbor no suspicion or anxiety; their body and mind will be peaceful and happy, and their spouse will be virtuous and faithful.
When their life comes to an end, they will not be oppressed by physical or mental suffering, but will be surrounded by their beloved wife, children, and kinsmen.
At the time of death, one will not see the terrifying messengers of King Yama;

instead, one will see only those who are pleasing to the mind—those who have perfected the well-disciplined Dharma, who possess the precepts, who are rich in virtue, and who are true fields of merit—serving as spiritual friends.
One’s body and mind will be filled with joy, and deep reverence and faith will arise.

Having passed away, they are reborn among human beings with all their faculties complete and their limbs fully formed; wherever they are born, they possess a full retinue of attendants, are handsome and intelligent, and enjoy peace and happiness.
Furthermore, they encounter a spiritual friend who is pleasing to the mind, one who has perfected the well-disciplined Dharma, is endowed with precepts, rich in virtue, and is a true field of merit.

Relying upon them for study and practice, they abandon sexual misconduct; they are able to sever all evil and unwholesome dharmas, accomplish all sublime wholesome dharmas, seek all the meanings of the Mahāyāna teachings, and cultivate all the vows and practices of a bodhisattva. Thus, they gradually enter the deep and vast ocean of wisdom, until finally attaining unsurpassed bodhi.
In the Buddha-land where he dwells, there are no women.
Sentient beings who have abandoned all lust and are fully endowed with the supreme Brahma-conduct come to be born in that land.
All sentient beings are born by transformation; they do not dwell in the foul, impure, and unclean state of the womb.
The Tathāgata’s own lifespan is immeasurable, and he teaches the Dharma to all sentient beings according to their needs.
After his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall abide for a long time, bringing benefit and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings.
“Good son! This is called the third wheel of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva for remaining far removed from sexual misconduct.
Because the bodhisattva-mahāsattva accomplishes this wheel, he attains freedom from error regarding the Śrāvaka Vehicle.”
He attains freedom from error regarding individuals of the Śrāvaka vehicle;
he attains freedom from error regarding the Pratyekabuddha vehicle;
and he attains freedom from error regarding individuals of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle.
They attain freedom from error regarding the Mahāyāna;
they attain freedom from error regarding individuals within the Mahāyāna.
They are always able to cause the lineage of the Triple Gem to blaze forth.

Regarding all disciples who have gone forth under the Tathāgatas—whether they be vessels of the Dharma or not, down to anyone who has donned even a fragment of the saṃghāṭī robe and shaved their hair and beard—one must never commit an error or offense against them.
Within the Mahāyāna Dharma, they shall always attain advancement and never regress;
their sharp wisdom and supreme merit shall constantly increase;
and regarding all meditative concentrations, dhāraṇīs, patiences, and stages, they shall swiftly attain mastery and never regress.
They always encounter various spiritual friends and act in accordance with them;
they never fail to see all Buddhas, nor to be with Bodhisattvas and Śrāvaka disciples; they never cease hearing the Dharma, nor ceasing to approach and make offerings to the Sangha;
regarding all roots of goodness, they always seek them with diligent effort, their minds never knowing satiety.
He is always insatiable in his mind regarding the various practices and vows for enlightenment.
The resulting rewards he attains are as extensively described previously. "Furthermore, good son!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able, for as long as life lasts, to abstain from false speech, all sentient beings will always love and respect them; whatever words they utter will be regarded as authoritative truth, and upon hearing them, all will reverently accept them without any suspicion.
By this means, these roots of goodness will quickly reach maturity.

All the obstacles to body, speech, and mind, the obstacles of afflictions, the obstacles of sentient beings, the obstacles to all dharmas, and the obstacles to trustworthy speech—created through false speech throughout the beginningless cycle of wandering in the five destinies and sinking in the river of birth and death; whether committed by oneself, incited in others, or rejoiced in upon seeing or hearing them—all such karmic hindrances are completely ground down, crushed, and extinguished without remainder by this wheel of abstaining from false speech, so that no retribution shall be experienced.

In this very life, all humans, devas, and others will hold them in common affection and harbor no suspicion; their body and mind will be peaceful and happy, and all others will faithfully believe whatever words they utter.
At the time of death, their body and mind will not be oppressed by sorrow or suffering, and they will be surrounded by their beloved wives, children, and kinsmen.
As they approach the end of life, they will not see the terrifying messengers of King Yama;

instead, they will see only those who are pleasing to them—those who have perfected the well-disciplined Dharma, who possess the precepts and abundant virtue, and who are true fields of merit—as their spiritual friends.
Their bodies and minds were filled with joy, and they conceived deep reverence and faith.

Having passed away, they were reborn among human beings, with all their faculties complete and their limbs fully formed. Wherever they were born, their speech was truthful, they were handsome and intelligent, and they lived in peace, security, and happiness.

Furthermore, they encounter a spiritual friend who is pleasing to the mind, one who has perfected the well-disciplined Dharma, is endowed with ethical precepts, rich in virtue, and is a true field of merit.

Relying upon them for study and practice, they abandon false speech; they are able to sever all evil and unwholesome dharmas, accomplish all sublime and wholesome dharmas, seek the meaning of all Mahāyāna teachings, and cultivate all the vows and practices of a bodhisattva. Thus, they gradually enter the deep and vast ocean of wisdom, until finally attaining unsurpassed enlightenment.
The Buddha-land where he dwells is entirely true and free from all falsehood;
it is adorned with exquisite fragrances and pure objects.

Sentient beings who are without flattery or deceit, whose mental conduct is upright and true, and who aspire to the purely wholesome Dharma, come to be born in that land, adorned with fragrant, pure, and exquisite garments and precious ornaments.

The Tathāgata’s own lifespan is immeasurable; he teaches the Dharma to all sentient beings as is appropriate, and after his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall abide for a long time, bringing benefit, peace, and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings.
"Good son! This is called the fourth wheel of the bodhisattva mahāsattva for remaining far removed from false speech.
Because the bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes this wheel, he attains freedom from error regarding the Śrāvaka Vehicle."
He is free from error regarding persons of the Śrāvaka vehicle;
he is free from error regarding the Pratyekabuddha vehicle;
and he is free from error regarding persons of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle.
They attain freedom from error regarding the Great Vehicle;
they attain freedom from error regarding individuals within the Great Vehicle.
They are always able to cause the lineage of the Three Jewels to blaze forth.

Regarding the ordained disciples of all Tathāgatas—whether they be vessels of the Dharma or not, down to anyone who has donned even a single fragment of the saffron robe and shaved their hair and beard—one must never commit an error or offense against them.
Within the Mahāyāna Dharma, they shall always attain advancement and never regress;
their sharp wisdom and supreme merit shall constantly increase;
and regarding all meditative concentrations, dhāraṇīs, patiences, and stages, they shall swiftly attain mastery and never regress.
They shall always encounter various spiritual friends and act in accordance with them;
they shall never be separated from the sight of all Buddhas, nor from Bodhisattvas and Śrāvaka disciples, nor from hearing the Dharma, nor from drawing near to and making offerings to the Sangha.
They constantly and diligently seek all roots of goodness with a mind that never knows satiety;
they are likewise never weary of the various practices and vows for enlightenment.
The resulting rewards are as extensively described before.
"Furthermore, good son!

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is able, for as long as life lasts, to abstain from divisive speech, all sentient beings will always love and respect him; whatever words he utters will be harmonious and conciliatory, and upon hearing them, they will all respectfully accept them without any suspicion."
By this means, one's roots of goodness quickly reach maturity.

All the karmic obstructions of body, speech, and mind, the obstructions of afflictions, the obstructions of sentient beings, the obstructions regarding all phenomena, and the obstructions to harmony and respect—which were created throughout the beginningless cycle of transmigration through the five destinies and sinking in the river of birth and death due to divisive speech—whether committed by oneself, incited in others, or rejoiced in upon seeing or hearing them performed, are all completely ground down, crushed, and utterly extinguished by this wheel of abstaining from divisive speech, such that no further retribution is experienced.

In this present life, all humans, devas, and others will hold them in common affection and harbor no suspicion or anxiety; their body and mind will be peaceful and happy, and every word they speak will be harmonious and compliant.
At the time of death, his body and mind will not be oppressed by sorrow or suffering, and he will be surrounded by his beloved wife, children, and kinsmen.
As he approaches the end of life, he will not see the terrifying messengers of King Yama;

instead, he will see only those who are pleasing to him—those who have perfected the well-disciplined Dharma, who possess the precepts, who are rich in virtue, and who are true fields of merit, serving as his spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra).
With body and mind filled with joy, they develop deep reverence and faith.
Having passed away, they are reborn among humans, with all faculties complete and limbs fully formed; wherever they are born, their speech is harmonious and agreeable.
They will be handsome and intelligent, living in peace and happiness.

Furthermore, they will encounter a spiritual friend who is pleasing to them—one who has mastered the well-disciplined Dharma, is endowed with precepts, is rich in virtue, and is a true field of merit.

By training in accordance with that, one abandons divisive speech, is able to sever all evil and unwholesome dharmas, is able to accomplish all sublime wholesome dharmas, is able to seek the meaning of all Mahāyāna teachings, and is able to cultivate all bodhisattva vows and practices; thus gradually entering the deep and vast ocean of wisdom, until finally attaining unsurpassed bodhi.
The Buddha-land where he dwells is entirely firm and dense, difficult to destroy, and adorned with all manner of exquisite things.
Sentient beings who are free from opposition and rivalry, who skillfully reconcile disputes, and who seek the pure and genuine wholesome Dharma come to be born in that land.
They shall constantly cultivate harmony and respect, and listen to the True Dharma.
The Tathāgata’s own lifespan shall be immeasurable, and he shall preach the Dharma to all sentient beings as is appropriate for them.
After his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain for a long time, bringing benefit, peace, and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings.
“Good son! This is called the fifth wheel of the bodhisattva mahāsattva: the complete abandonment of divisive speech.
Because the bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes this wheel, he attains freedom from error regarding the Śrāvaka vehicle.”
They attain freedom from error regarding persons of the Śrāvaka vehicle;
they attain freedom from error regarding the Pratyekabuddha vehicle;
and they attain freedom from error regarding persons of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle.
They attain freedom from error regarding the Mahāyāna;
they attain freedom from error regarding individuals within the Mahāyāna.
They are always able to cause the lineage of the Three Jewels to blaze forth.

Regarding the ordained disciples of all Tathāgatas—whether they be vessels of the Dharma or not vessels of the Dharma, down to anyone who has donned even a fragment of the saffron robe and shaved their hair and beard—one must never commit an error or offense against them.
Within the Mahāyāna Dharma, they shall always attain advancement and never regress;
their sharp wisdom and supreme merit shall constantly increase;
and regarding all meditative concentrations, dhāraṇīs, patiences, and stages, they shall swiftly attain mastery and never regress.
They always encounter various spiritual friends and act in accordance with them;
they never fail to see all Buddhas, nor to be with bodhisattvas and śrāvaka disciples; they never cease hearing the Dharma, nor ceasing to approach and make offerings to the Sangha;
regarding all roots of goodness, they always seek them with diligence, their minds never wearying or satisfied.
He is always insatiable in his mind regarding the various practices and vows for enlightenment.
The resulting rewards he attains are as extensively described previously. "Furthermore, good son!

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is able to refrain from harsh and evil speech for as long as they live, all sentient beings will always love and respect them; whatever words they utter will cause everyone to rejoice, and upon hearing them, all will receive them with reverence and harbor no suspicion.
By this means, one's roots of goodness quickly reach maturity.

Whatever obstacles to the body, speech, and mind, obstacles of affliction, obstacles regarding sentient beings, obstacles regarding all phenomena, and obstacles regarding discipline and goodness—one has created throughout the beginningless cycle of transmigration through the five destinies while submerged in the river of birth and death—whether committed by oneself, incited in others, or rejoiced in upon seeing or hearing them, are all completely ground down, crushed, and extinguished without remainder by this wheel of abstaining from harsh speech; thus, their karmic retribution is no longer received.

In this very life, all humans, devas, and others will hold them in common affection and harbor no suspicion; their body and mind will be peaceful and happy, and every word they utter will bring joy to others.
At the time of death, his body and mind will not be oppressed by sorrow or suffering, and he will be surrounded by his beloved wife, children, and kinsmen.
As he approaches the end of life, he will not see the terrifying messengers of King Yama;

instead, he will behold as spiritual friends those who are pleasing to him, who have perfected the well-disciplined Dharma, who are endowed with precepts and rich in virtue, and who are true fields of merit.
With body and mind filled with joy, they develop deep reverence and faith.

After their lives have ended, they are reborn among human beings, with all faculties complete and limbs fully formed; wherever they are born, their speech is gentle, they are handsome and intelligent, and they dwell in peace and happiness.
Furthermore, they encounter a spiritual friend who is pleasing to the mind, one who has perfected the well-disciplined Dharma, is endowed with precepts, rich in virtue, and is a true field of merit.

Relying upon them for study and practice, they abandon coarse and evil speech; they are able to sever all evil and unwholesome dharmas, accomplish all sublime wholesome dharmas, seek the meaning of all Mahāyāna teachings, and cultivate all the vows and practices of a bodhisattva. Thus, they gradually enter the deep and vast ocean of wisdom, until finally attaining unsurpassed bodhi.
The Buddha-land where he dwells is far removed from all unpleasant sounds;
rather, it is filled with various sublime, wish-fulfilling, harmonious, and elegant sounds that accord with the inclinations of beings, as well as the sounds of the compilation of the Dharma.

Sentient beings who are endowed with mindfulness and wisdom, whose Brahma-voices are clear and penetrating, and who are disciplined and virtuous, will be born in that land; they shall always encourage one another with gentle speech.
The Tathāgata himself possesses immeasurable lifespan and teaches the Dharma to all sentient beings according to their needs.
After his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall abide for a long time, bringing benefit, peace, and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings.
Son of good family!
This is called the sixth wheel of the bodhisattva mahāsattva: the distancing from harsh and evil speech.
“Because the bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes this wheel, he is free from error regarding the Śrāvaka vehicle;
he is free from error regarding individuals of the Śrāvaka vehicle;
and he is free from error regarding the Pratyekabuddha vehicle.”
He becomes free from error regarding individuals belonging to the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle;
he becomes free from error regarding the Mahāyāna;
and he becomes free from error regarding individuals belonging to the Mahāyāna.
They are always able to cause the lineage of the Triple Gem to flourish;

regarding all disciples of the Tathāgatas who have gone forth—whether they be vessels of the Dharma or not, down to those who merely wear a fragment of the kāṣāya and have shaved their hair and beards—they act without error or failure.

Whatever obstacles of physical, verbal, and mental unwholesome karma, obstacles of afflictions, obstacles regarding sentient beings, obstacles regarding all phenomena, and obstacles regarding meaningful benefits—one has created throughout the beginningless cycle of transmigrating through the five destinies and sinking in the river of birth and death due to frivolous speech—whether committed by oneself, incited in others, or rejoiced in upon seeing or hearing them performed, are all completely ground down, crushed, and extinguished without remainder by this wheel of abstaining from frivolous speech, such that no karmic retribution is experienced.

In this very life, all humans, devas, and others will hold them in common affection and harbor no suspicion; their body and mind will be peaceful and happy, and every word they utter will be meaningful and beneficial.
At the time of death, his body and mind will not be oppressed by sorrow or suffering, and he will be surrounded by his beloved wife, children, and kinsmen.
As he approaches the end of life, he will not see the terrifying messengers of King Yama;

instead, he will behold as spiritual friends those who are pleasing to him—those who have perfected the well-disciplined Dharma, are endowed with precepts, are rich in virtue, and are true fields of merit.
With body and mind filled with joy, they give rise to profound reverence and faith.

Upon the end of their lives, they are reborn among humans, with all faculties complete and limbs fully formed; wherever they are born, their speech is invariably beneficial, and they are handsome, intelligent, peaceful, and happy.
Furthermore, they encounter a spiritual friend who is pleasing to the mind, one who has mastered the well-disciplined Dharma, is endowed with precepts, rich in virtue, and is a true field of merit.

Relying upon them for study and practice, they abandon frivolous speech; they are able to sever all evil and unwholesome dharmas, accomplish all sublime and wholesome dharmas, seek the meaning of all Mahāyāna teachings, and cultivate all the vows and practices of a bodhisattva. Thus, they gradually enter the deep and vast ocean of wisdom, until finally attaining unsurpassed enlightenment.
The Buddha-land where he dwells is far removed from all sounds that are meaningless or unbeneficial;
rather, the sounds of the various sublime Dharma teachings, subsumed within the Bodhisattva-piṭaka, pervade the entire realm.
Sentient beings who have accomplished boundless great vows and sublime wisdom, and who are skillfully able to explain the various meanings of the Dharma, come to be born in that land.

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva accomplishes these ten wheels, they can swiftly realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. Why is this so?

In past ages, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas were entirely free from the ten paths of unwholesome action, and they all extolled and praised the fruits and rewards obtained through these ten paths of wholesome action.
It is for the sake of nurturing all sentient beings, providing them with benefit, peace, and the path to enlightenment;
it is for the sake of eliminating the suffering of karma and afflictions of all sentient beings so that none remains;
and it is for the sake of drying up the three evil realms of existence.
For the sake of perpetuating the lineage of the Triple Gem;
for the sake of severing existence within the three realms;
and for the sake of forever ending the aggregates, elements, and sense bases.
It is for the sake of causing all beings to swiftly enter the city of fearless nirvana;
the detailed exposition is as previously described regarding the karmic fruits obtained from abandoning the ten unwholesome paths of action.
Therefore, son of good family!

If one does not sincerely seek the fruit of Buddhahood realized through these ten paths of wholesome action, nor sincerely protect even a single path of wholesome action until the end of life, yet claims for oneself:
"I am a true practitioner of the Mahāyāna; I seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"You should know that such a person is utterly deceitful and a great liar.

Before the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions, they delude the world; being shameless and without remorse, they preach the views of nihilism and annihilationism to entice and deceive the ignorant;
when their bodies perish and their lives end, they fall into the various evil realms."

“Good son! If one could attain bodhi and enter parinirvāṇa merely through verbal discourse or mere hearing, without practicing the ten paths of wholesome action, then in a single kalpa or even in a single moment, one could cause all sentient beings—as numerous as the atoms of the earth in all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions—to ascend to perfect enlightenment and enter parinirvāṇa; yet such a thing is impossible.”
Why is this? The ten paths of wholesome action are the root of the Mahāyāna, the cause of bodhi, and the firm ladder for realizing nirvāṇa.
O son of good family!

If one could attain bodhi and enter parinirvāṇa merely by generating the mind of awakening and the power of vows, without practicing the ten paths of wholesome action, then within a single eon or even a single moment, one might cause all sentient beings—as numerous as the atoms and lands of all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions—to ascend to perfect enlightenment and enter parinirvāṇa; yet such a thing is impossible.
Why is this? The ten paths of wholesome action are the root of the merit of both mundane and supramundane, extraordinary fruits and rewards. Good son!

If one does not practice the ten paths of wholesome action, even if one passes through as many eons as there are atoms in all the Buddha-lands of the ten directions—whether self-proclaiming oneself a Mahāyāna practitioner, or preaching, or listening, or merely generating the aspiration for enlightenment, or making vows—one will ultimately be unable to realize bodhi and nirvāṇa, nor will one enable others to escape the suffering of birth and death.

“Good son! It is only through the practice of the ten paths of wholesome action that there exist in the world the great and wealthy lineages of kṣatriyas and brahmins; from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-perception; or the vehicle of the śrāvakas, or the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, up to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—all these arise from the various distinctions in the practice of the ten paths of wholesome action.”
Therefore, son of good family!
If you wish to swiftly fulfill the vow for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, you should cultivate these ten paths of wholesome action to adorn yourself;
one who dwells in the ten unwholesome actions and lacks moral discipline cannot fulfill such a great vow for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

If one seeks to swiftly awaken to the state of the Mahāyāna, swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and swiftly fulfill all vows for wholesome dharmas, one should first protect and uphold the ten paths of virtuous action.

Why is this so? Because the ten paths of wholesome action are the root for establishing all virtuous qualities and merits, and they are the cause for the superior fruits and rewards of both the mundane and supramundane realms.
"Therefore, you should cultivate the ten paths of wholesome action.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to further clarify this meaning, spoke in verse:
