Entrusting the Benefits The Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra on the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha, Chapter Eight: Entrusting the Benefits. When the Buddha had thus spoken this great Dharma gate, there were among the assembly Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges who, having long practiced the mindfulness and contemplation of the Buddha in the past, now, upon hearing the World-Honored One’s teaching on the skillful means for cultivating the visualization of the Buddha through mindfulness, all attained the samādhi-gate of mindfulness of the Buddha.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing this Dharma, all attained the *sarva-samādhi-jīvita-mālā-dhāraṇī* gate.
Again, there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing what the Buddha had spoken, all attained the *sarva-śūraṅgama-vaidyutāloka-niśraya-dhāraṇī* gate.

Furthermore, there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing what the Buddha had spoken, all attained the light of dependent origination for mastery over all dharmas and the patience of conformity (*ānulomikī kṣānti*).

Again, there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing what the Buddha had spoken, became free from dust and removed from defilement, giving rise to the pure Dharma-eye regarding all dharmas and attaining the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*).
Furthermore, there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing what the Buddha taught, attained the fruit of once-returning (sakṛdāgāmin).
Again, there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing what the Buddha taught, attained the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmin).
Furthermore, there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing what the Buddha taught, all attained the supreme fruit of arhatship.

Moreover, there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing what the Buddha taught, resolved in their hearts to escape the prison of the triple world; they left the household life in reliance upon the Buddha and entered the true Dharma.

Furthermore, there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing what the Buddha had taught, dwelt throughout their lives in the path of the ten wholesome karmic actions and, relying on the Śrāvaka Vehicle, resolved their minds toward awakening without ever regressing.

Furthermore, there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing what the Buddha had taught, dwelt throughout their lives in the ten paths of wholesome action and resolved to follow the Pratyekabuddha vehicle with non-retrogressive resolve.

Furthermore, there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing what the Buddha had taught, dwelt throughout their lives in the path of the ten virtuous actions and, relying on the Mahāyāna, gave rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, never again to regress.

Furthermore, there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing what the Buddha had spoken, attained the right view of the world. By means of this right view, they eliminated all afflictions and evil karmas that serve as causes for rebirth in the evil realms, and they increased all virtuous vows and wholesome karmas that serve as causes for rebirth in the auspicious realms.

Furthermore, there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing what the Buddha had taught, all received the three refuges, dwelt securely in the status of lay devotees (*upāsaka*), and abided in the pure precepts of the near-dweller (*upavāsa*). They delighted in making offerings to the Buddha, delighting in hearing the Dharma, and delighting in serving the Saṃgha; they applied themselves with diligence day and night, never once becoming weary or negligent.

Furthermore, there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing what the Buddha had spoken, distanced themselves from all wrong paths, false refuges, evil intentions, and evil karma; they attained resolute faith within the Buddha-dharma, renounced the ways of the household life, and left home for the pure life of a monastic.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, saying:
"O son of good family!
I now entrust this Dharma-gate of the Great Seal of the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha into your hands; you should receive and uphold it, and cause it to be widely disseminated."

If there are sentient beings who, regarding this Dharma-gate, are able to read and recite it, contemplate its meaning, explain it to others, and abide in right practice, you should protect them with ten dharmas, so that they may enjoy benefit and happiness throughout the long night.
What are the ten? First, for their protection, ensuring that all their wealth and status remain free from loss or deficiency;
second, for their protection, ensuring that no enemies cause them harm.
Third, to protect them so that they may abandon all wrong views, false refuges, and the ten paths of unwholesome action;
fourth, to protect them so that they may avoid all bodily, verbal, and punitive retributions;
fifth, to protect them by obstructing and severing all slander, defamation, and derision.
Sixth, for their protection, to ensure they remain unoffending in all rules of conduct and ethical discipline (*śīla*);
seventh, for their protection, to cause the total eradication of all non-human spirits, disturbances of the four elements, and untimely aging or illness;
eighth, for their protection, to prevent them from encountering any untimely, irrational calamities or premature deaths.
Ninth, through that protection, when their life is about to end, they shall behold the physical forms of all Buddhas;
tenth, through that protection, after their death, they shall be reborn in a happy realm, experiencing benefit, peace, and happiness.

"Good son! If there are sentient beings who, regarding this dharma-gate, are able to read and recite it, contemplate its meaning, explain it to others, and abide in right practice, you should diligently protect them in these ten ways, so that they may experience benefit and happiness throughout the long night."
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja addressed the Buddha, saying:
“So be it, World-Honored One!
I shall receive and uphold such a dharma-gate and cause it to be widely disseminated.”

If there are sentient beings who are able to read, recite, contemplate the meaning of, explain to others, and abide in the correct practice of this Dharma-gate, I shall protect them with ten dharmas, so that they may experience benefit and happiness throughout the long night.

The *Daśacakrakṣitigarbha-sūtra* is a teaching for the Dharma-ending age (mofa) in this land.
How is this made clear?

The Buddha taught that in this evil time of the Dharma-ending age, when the sages have long since departed, those with ruined faculties are compared to fragile earthenware; those with empty views are likened to one born blind; those who are intoxicated by the five desires are similar to a fallow field that does not sprout; and those who run wild with the ten non-virtues resemble the filth and impurities of a stinking body.

Therefore, this sutra can wash away the foul body, open the eyes of the blind, mold the unbaked clay vessel, and irrigate the stony field. For this reason, the Bodhisattva manifests in the form of a Śrāvaka, and the Elephant King honors the robes of renunciation; through these banner-like signs, he transforms those who lack shame, reveals the protection of the two matters, and brings to fruition the path and fruits of the three vehicles.
Therefore, the Sūtra says:
"In order that the lineage of the Three Jewels in this land may flourish with majestic power and abide long in the world.
It further says:

Thus, the Three Jewels shall endure for a long time, and the manifest teaching shall be transmitted during the Dharma-Ending Age; yet these adamantine afflictions serve as obstacles that differ from those encountered on the Single Vehicle (Ekayāna).
